  • translucentRectLights (false): whether a rectangle light lights the surface as a rectangle. Off, it lights it as a point light at its centre and the translucent programs hold none of the rectangle shading; opaque surfaces always take the rectangle.
// Glass under a lamp is shadowed by what stands between them: one sample of each light's map.
const world = createWorld('viewer', { shadowTranslucentLocalLights: true })
// And with the penumbra the opaque surfaces get, for every translucent pixel.
const fine = createWorld('viewer', {
  shadowTranslucentQuality: 1,
  shadowTranslucentLocalLights: true,
})
// A rectangle light lights glass as the rectangle it is.
const panels = createWorld('viewer', { translucentRectLights: true })

A material can ask more of its own, whatever the switches say, at their defaults of false and 0: translucentDirectionalLightShadowQuality above 0 takes the full trace for the sun's shadow on its surfaces, translucentLocalLightShadow shadows the local lights on them, and translucentLocalLightShadowQuality above 0 takes the full trace for those lights. A scene whose surfaces ask nothing pays nothing: the translucent programs hold none of that code.

// One pane of glass reads the sun's shadow with the full trace, the rest of the scene with one sample.
material.meshStandard({
  transparent: true,
  opacity: 0.3,
  translucentDirectionalLightShadowQuality: 1,
})
// A lantern's glass is shadowed by the lamps around it, one sample of each map.
material.meshStandard({ transparent: true, translucentLocalLightShadow: true })
// And with the full trace for those lamps.
material.meshStandard({
  transparent: true,
  translucentLocalLightShadow: true,
  translucentLocalLightShadowQuality: 1,
})

A light shadows a translucent surface only while it casts (castsShadow) and the shadows are on (shadowQuality past 0). The shadows of the fog and of the air are their own reads: these switches do not touch them.

Reference: world.shadows.

light-follows-exposure.title: A light that follows the exposure
light-follows-exposure.description: Divide a light's strength by the image's exposure with inverseExposureBlend.
light-follows-exposure.html:
A point, a spot or a rectangle light holds inverseExposureBlend (0, from 0 to 1): how much its strength is divided by the image's exposure. At 0 the light keeps its strength whatever the exposure; at 1 it is divided by it, so it looks the same in a dark scene as in a bright one, as a lit sign does under the automatic exposure; between, the geometric blend, the exposure to the power of minus the number. A directional light has none (setting one is refused, INVALID_SCENE_LIGHT). The value is saved with the world. The buffer keeps the light's own strength; every pass that reads it — the lights, the fog, the translucent surfaces, the surface cache — applies the blend there, with the exposure of the view it draws, so two views at two exposures each see their own.

const sign = light.point({ intensity: 800, inverseExposureBlend: 1 }) // looks as bright in the dark as in the day
sign.inverseExposureBlend = 0.5 // half-way, the next frame

light-distance-culling.title: A light that is left out at a distance
light-distance-culling.description: A light that spans too little of the screen, or lies past its distance, is left out: the options that decide.
light-distance-culling.html:
In a perspective view a point, a spot or a rectangle light is left out of the image, its lighting and its shadow both, when it spans too little of the screen, or lies past its own distance. Its bounding sphere has a radius W (metres) and lies at the distance d from the view: the light is drawn while min(0.02, lightMinScreenRadius / W) * factor * d < 1 (so a light of 1.5 m or less, or of no size, is dropped past 50 m, a larger one past W / 0.03), and, when its maxDrawDistance (0, no limit, in metres) is above 0, while d < maxDrawDistance * lightMaxDrawDistanceScale (a scale of 0 drops every light that names a distance). factor is the view's horizontal field of view in degrees over 90 (a zoomed view keeps its lights farther away), or 1 where lightDrawRangeFollowsFieldOfView is false. The three view settings are lightMinScreenRadius (0.03), lightMaxDrawDistanceScale (1) and lightDrawRangeFollowsFieldOfView (true), written with the view's shadow settings (world.shadows, each frame). A directional light and an orthographic view always draw. A directional light refuses maxDrawDistance (INVALID_SCENE_LIGHT). The value is saved with the world.

const lamp = light.point({ intensity: 20, distance: 8, maxDrawDistance: 120 }) // gone past 120 m
lamp.maxDrawDistance = 0 // no limit again, the next frame
world.shadows = { lightMinScreenRadius: 0.06 } // small lights are dropped twice as near

Reference: world.shadows.

lighting-channels.title: Lighting channels
lighting-channels.description: Three lighting channels decide which light lights which object.
lighting-channels.html:
A light lights an object only if they share a lighting channel. There are three, channel0, channel1 and channel2, and every object and every light is in channel 0 alone by default, so by default every light lights every object. Both hold lightingChannels, a set of three booleans (saved with the world): a whole set is written, the set read is frozen, and a set missing a channel, or holding anything but booleans, is refused (RangeError for an object, INVALID_SCENE_LIGHT for a light). A set with no channel is legal: an object in none is lit by no light, a light in none lights nothing.

// A lamp that lights the scenery in channel 1 alone, and a prop in channels 0 and 1 that every light reaches.
const lamp = light.point({ lightingChannels: { channel0: false, channel1: true, channel2: false } })
scenery.lightingChannels = { channel0: false, channel1: true, channel2: false }
prop.lightingChannels = { channel0: true, channel1: true, channel2: false }
lamp.lightingChannels = { channel0: true, channel1: true, channel2: false } // a write reaches the lights at once

The channels act on the direct light of the opaque surfaces and of the see-through surfaces lit in the forward pass (translucencyLighting: 'forward', the water, the transmissive layers); the translucency lighting volume, the fog and the indirect light do not read them. A scene whose lights and objects are all in channel 0 compiles its lighting without the test.

translucency-lighting-volume.title: A see-through surface lit from the translucency lighting volume
translucency-lighting-volume.description: A volume built round the camera each image that lights the blended surfaces in one read: its settings.
translucency-lighting-volume.html:
A blended surface takes the light of a volume the engine builds round the camera each image, one read for the pixel in place of every light (translucencyLighting):

  • 'volumetricNonDirectional' (the default of a material made in code): the volume's light, as a medium takes it, from its constant light alone, the same whatever the surface's normal: no reflection.
  • 'volumetric': the volume's light, as a medium takes it, weighed by the surface's normal: no reflection.
  • 'volume': the volume's light, as a surface takes it, and the reflection of the environment kept. A blended material imported from a scene file is given this one.
  • 'forward': every light read for the pixel, its shadow and its highlight included. A material imported from a scene file that transmits (KHR_materials_transmission) is given this one.

In the three volume modes (a volume is built whenever a blended surface wears one of them, which is the default) the surface gives back the volume's light on its diffuse colour (none for a metal), in a normal or additive layer of the default lit model or the thin subsurface. The mode alone says what lights a layer, whatever its blending mode: a layer of another blending mode (alphaComposite, alphaHoldout, multiply, subtractive), and a layer of any other shading model (the skin, the subsurface profile, the eye, the hair), is lit by no light of its own in a volume mode: it takes nothing of the volume and no highlight from the lights, and keeps the light the bounce and the environment give it, as a forward surface does. Only 'forward' reads every light. A shadow catcher and a transmissive (refracting) surface keep their forward lighting whatever the mode. A scene none of whose surfaces asks for a volume the volume lights makes none, nor does an image that draws no such layer: no pass runs, no texture is made and the programs hold none of its code; a surface whose mode is changed redraws the session's blended programs.

The fog of a see-through surface: per vertex or per pixel

The fog a see-through surface is seen through is worked out for each vertex and interpolated, from the farthest layer to the nearest: the height fog (or the distance fog) with the haze of the air behind it, the local fog volumes of the tile the vertex lies in over them, and the clouds over those where the material has cloudFog. The fog's volume is always read for the pixel and laid over it, the local fog volumes of a pixel under it. A scene none of whose see-through surfaces takes its fog per vertex (all computeFogPerPixel, water or fog: false) compiles its programs without the vertex fog. A material with computeFogPerPixel: true (false by default) works the whole fog out for each pixel instead: exact, and dearer, for a large triangle or a surface near the fog's start. Single-layer water is always per pixel.

material.meshStandard({ transparent: true, opacity: 0.3, computeFogPerPixel: true }) // a large pane, fogged exactly
material.meshStandard({ transparent: true, opacity: 0.4, translucencyLighting: 'forward' }) // every light read for the pixel
material.meshStandard({ transparent: true, opacity: 0.4, translucencyLighting: 'volume' }) // a pane lit by the volume
material.meshStandard({ transparent: true, opacity: 0.2, translucencyLighting: 'volumetric' }) // smoke or a veil
material.meshStandard({
  transparent: true,
  opacity: 0.2,
  translucencyLighting: 'volumetricNonDirectional',
}) // a glow lit the same on every side

A double-sided see-through surface (side: 'double') is drawn in one pass that culls neither face, as every two-sided surface is. twoSidedPasses (boolean, false by default) asks two passes instead, its back faces then its front faces, so a closed shape (a bottle, a bubble) shows its far side through its near one in the right order, for twice the draws of the surface in the blend pass:

// A bubble drawn back faces first, then front faces.
material.meshStandard({ transparent: true, opacity: 0.3, side: 'double', twoSidedPasses: true })

The volume is two nested cascades of cubes of cells that follow the camera: the inner one holds the view to translucencyVolumeInnerDistance metres, the outer one the stretch from there to translucencyVolumeOuterDistance; their centres are snapped to a whole number of cells, so that the light does not crawl as the camera moves. Each image the sun and every local light that reaches a cascade are injected into its cells, each by its own shadow map read at the cell (the sun with its light function, the clouds' shade and the air's tint; a local light with its fall-off and its light function); the light is kept as a two-band spherical harmonic, so a surface reads the light's direction too. A cell whose shadow no virtual shadow map holds a page for reads its light unshadowed. A surface past the outer cascade reads the sun unshadowed and no local light. The cells are then blended with the image before (translucencyVolumeTemporal) and blurred (translucencyVolumeBlur), and the surfaces read them by eight loads and a blend of the two cascades. The settings are the reference's, each an option of createWorld too, held over the quality preset, changed later from the next frame (packages/sdk-core/src/contracts/translucencyVolumeOptions.ts); a value a setting does not take is refused:

FieldMeaningDefault
translucencyVolumeWhether the volume is made; off, a surface that reads it reads blacktrue
translucencyVolumeDimCells a side of each cascade, 4 to 2048 (held to what the device's 3D textures hold)64
translucencyVolumeInnerDistanceMetres from the camera the inner cascade ends at15
translucencyVolumeOuterDistanceMetres from the camera the outer cascade ends at50
translucencyVolumeBlurThe spatial filter: each cell is the mean of eight trilinear reads round it; it runs after the temporal blend where that is ontrue
translucencyVolumeTemporalEach cell is blended with the same point of the volume of the image before, ahead of the blurfalse
translucencyVolumeHistoryWeightThe share of that history kept, 0 to 10.9
translucencyVolumePositionOffsetRadiusCells: the radius of a noise, different for each pixel and image, that moves the point a surface reads the volume at; 0 none0
translucencyVolumeAdaptToPerspectiveThe cascades are sized by the camera's own field of view and aspect, not a field of 45 degrees and a square viewfalse
translucencyVolumeMinFovDegrees: the least field of view the cascades follow while the setting above is on45
translucencyVolumeFovSnapDegrees: the field is rounded up to a multiple of it, which makes the volume jump in steps as the field animates10
translucencyVolumeMarkVoxelsOnly the cells the surfaces read (8 per fetch, dilated by a cell) are marked, lit and filteredfalse

The quality presets write the cells' count and the blur: smooth 24 cells and no blur, balanced 32 and no blur, fine and cinematic nothing. A volume of the default size holds 16 MiB of textures (two half-float textures of the light as injected, and the packed volume the surfaces read); with the temporal filter on it holds two more such volumes, 24 MiB with no blur and 32 with it; the device's memory budget may refuse them, and the surfaces then read black.

const world = createWorld('viewer', { translucencyVolumeDim: 32 }) // a coarser volume
world.translucencyVolume = {
  translucencyVolumeInnerDistance: 30,
  translucencyVolumeOuterDistance: 120,
} // a larger reach, from the next frame
world.translucencyVolume = {
  translucencyVolumeTemporal: true,
  translucencyVolumeHistoryWeight: 0.8,
} // blend with the image before
world.translucencyVolume = { translucencyVolumeDim: null } // given back to the preset
world.translucencyVolume = { translucencyVolumeMarkVoxels: true } // light only the cells the surfaces read
world.translucencyVolume = { translucencyVolume: false } // off: no pass, no texture, no byte

The explorer takes the same by field (explorer.setTranslucencyVolume('translucencyVolumeDim', 48)), and an agent through trillion3d_set_translucency_volume.

translucency-global-illumination-volume.title: Translucency global illumination volume
translucency-global-illumination-volume.description: The grid that holds the indirect light of the see-through surfaces: cell size, depth slices and options.
translucency-global-illumination-volume.html:
The indirect light of the see-through surfaces (blend, water, transmission) is held in a grid fitted to the view: a cell is translucencyGiGridPixelSize pixels a side across the image, and its depth slices follow a logarithm of the distance from the camera out to translucencyGiEndDistance. Each image every cell traces translucencyGiTracingResolution squared cones (the global distance field marched, the surface cache read at the hit, the radiance cache read for what the march leaves), the light is filtered along the three axes, projected on two-band harmonics and blended with the volume of the image before; a surface reads it with one filtered fetch, instead of gathering the world's probes in each fragment. The cells read the world's radiance cache, translucencyGiRadianceCacheClipmapBias cascades coarser than the one covering them. The grid needs the screen probes' levels that cast probes; below them, and with the setting off, a surface takes the sky light irradiance alone. Settings (packages/sdk-core/src/contracts/translucencyGiOptions.ts), distances in metres:

SettingMeaningDefault
translucencyGiWhether the volume is madetrue
translucencyGiTraceFromVolumeThe cells march the distance field before reading the cachetrue
translucencyGiHardwareRayTracingWith the march on, cast the cones through the scene's trianglestrue
translucencyGiRadianceCacheThe cells read the radiance cachetrue
translucencyGiRadianceCacheClipmapBiasCascades coarser than the covering one for reads and marks3
translucencyGiGridPixelSizePixels a side of a cell32
translucencyGiGridDistributionLogZScalePer metre, the slices' logarithm scale1
translucencyGiGridDistributionLogZOffsetThe logarithm's offset1
translucencyGiGridDistributionZScaleSlices per doubling of the depth4
translucencyGiEndDistanceMetres, the depth of the last slice80
translucencyGiTracingResolutionCones a cell traces along a side3
translucencyGiMaxRayIntensityThe brightest a cone may be, in exposure units20
translucencyGiGridCenterOffsetFromDepthBufferCells a trace point behind the depth is held in front of it; <0 none0.5
translucencyGiOffsetThresholdToAcceptDepthBufferOffsetCells, the nearest behind the depth a point is moved forward from1
translucencyGiSpatialFilterFilter the cones' light along the three axestrue
translucencyGiSpatialFilterSampleCountCells either side of the filter centre3
translucencyGiSpatialFilterStandardDeviationCells, the filter's Gaussian5
translucencyGiTemporalReprojectionBlend with the image before, reprojectedtrue
translucencyGiTemporalJitterTurn the trace point and directions each imagetrue
translucencyGiTemporalHistoryWeightShare of the history kept0.9
translucencyGiTemporalMaxRayDirectionsTurns the directions take before they come round8
 
const world = createWorld('viewer', { translucencyGiGridPixelSize: 16 }) // finer cells
world.translucencyGi = { translucencyGiEndDistance: 150 } // a deeper grid, from the next frame
world.translucencyGi = { translucencyGiTemporalHistoryWeight: null } // given back to its default
world.translucencyGi = { translucencyGiHardwareRayTracing: false } // keep marching the distance field
world.translucencyGi = { translucencyGi: false } // off: no pass, no texture

The explorer takes the same by field (explorer.setTranslucencyGi('translucencyGiEndDistance', 120)), and an agent through trillion3d_set_translucency_gi.

single-layer-water.title: Single-layer water
single-layer-water.description: A body of water seen through one layer: the four water outputs, the options of its look and its cost.
single-layer-water.html:
A lit surface whose material graph wires any of the four water outputs (scatteringCoefficients, absorptionCoefficients, phaseG, colorScaleBehindWater, the first two per centimetre) is a body of water seen through one layer. It is drawn over the opaque scene, after the lights and before every translucent layer, in the passes the reference's single-layer water has: the scene without the water is copied (its depth as the distance along the view, its colour), the water's depth is drawn first, then the water is shaded over the copy — its surface lit by the declared lights as a physical surface, the base material's colour under the coverage its opacity output gives (1: the base material only, 0: pure water), the volume between the surface and the scene behind it integrated analytically — and last the reflection of the surface is added. The volume is the sun's in-scattering (a phase function of phaseG in the direction the refraction bends the view to; the sun is the forward directional light) and the ambient light's, over the share of the light the volume scatters before it absorbs it, less the Fresnel reflectance of the surface; what lies behind is read where the surface refracts it (the surface normal bent by the index of refraction, from the surface's specular, or the refraction output when it is wired), dimmed by the colour absorption over the depth of water and by the fall from the scene to the water's height, and multiplied by colorScaleBehindWater. The reflection is the transparents' front layer's trace — the engine's reflection of the nearest transparent surface, traced as the opaque one is — weighed on the surface's reflectance, faded in over the first 50 cm of water above the scene, always traced for the water whatever reflectionFrontLayer says (at every level that traces reflections). The water's depth becomes the scene's: fog, particles and the transparents drawn after are hidden behind it.

Reflection hit lighting

Options of the reflections (packages/sdk-core/src/contracts/hitLightingOptions.ts), each with the reference's default. A reflection ray that meets the scene's triangles reads the light the surface cache holds at the hit. With reflectionHardwareRayTracingHitLighting: true the hits the cache cannot light (no card gave any light) are collected, sorted by material (reflectionHardwareRayTracingBucketMaterials, on; the key is a hash of what makes the shading of a material differ) and lit where they stand: the hit's own material under the scene's lights (hardwareRayTracingHitLightingDirectLighting on): its whole response toward the eye, the diffuse and the specular lobe, times a shadow ray each (hardwareRayTracingHitLightingShadowMode 'off', 'hard' or 'soft'), plus the emitted light and the indirect light: the surface cache's, or the sky light's irradiance with hardwareRayTracingHitLightingSkylight: 'on', where hardwareRayTracingHitLightingReflectionCaptures: true makes the specular share the material's reflectance on the sky light's filtered cube along the reflected ray. With the direct lighting off and no sky light the surface cache's own light is read as it stands; off with the sky light, the hit has the sky light's terms alone. hardwareRayTracingLightingMode: 'hitLighting' (or 'hitLightingForReflections') lights every hit of the reflections this way; 'hitLighting' alone also lights, this way, the hits of the screen probes' rays (screenProbeHardwareRayTracing) and of the radiance cache's rays (the other two modes keep the surface cache for them); hardwareRayTracingHitLightingAllowed (on) is the switch that forbids it all; hardwareRayTracingHitLightingForceOpaque (off) makes the trace that meets the hit again skip the masks' any-hit test; hardwareRayTracingHitLightingShadowTranslucencyMode sets what the shadow rays cut: 'opaque' every surface, 'masked' (the default) the masked ones by their alpha and none of the translucent ones, 'fractional' the masked ones and, through the translucent ones, the share their coverage lets through.

const world = await createWorld({
  reflections: {
    reflectionHardwareRayTracingHitLighting: true,
    hardwareRayTracingHitLightingShadowMode: 'hard',
  },
})
world.reflections = { hardwareRayTracingLightingMode: 'hitLighting' } // every hit lit where it stands, from the next frame

With hardwareRayTracingLightingMode: 'hitLighting' the rays of the screen probes (screenProbeHardwareRayTracing, with the scene's triangles traced) light their hits the same way: the stage that casts them marks each hit on a triangle with the key of its material, the marks are collected and sorted by material (reflectionHardwareRayTracingBucketMaterials), and the hit is lit where it stands — the material, the lights and their shadow rays, the sun's shadow ray running as far as screenProbeMaxTraceDistance — plus the surface cache's indirect light (or the sky light's, hardwareRayTracingHitLightingSkylight: 'on'), the sky light that leaks onto the hit and the height fog laid over the ray. The probes' rays have one bounce, no refraction and no reflection capture whatever reflectionMaxBounces and the other path settings say; a hit on the back of a surface that is not two-sided ends the ray with no light. The buffers hold 80 bytes for each ray of the view (8 for its entry in the list of hits, 8 for its sorted copy and 64 for the radiance of its path); where the radiance no longer fits one storage binding of the device the mode is refused with a line in the console, and where the device's memory budget leaves no room for the buffers the probes keep the surface cache's light for the image, the mode staying as set.

world.reflections = { hardwareRayTracingLightingMode: 'hitLighting' } // reflections and screen probes alike

The radiance cache's rays light their hits the same way (screenProbeRadianceCacheHardwareRayTracing, with the scene's triangles traced; the same 'hitLighting' mode, the other two keep the surface cache's light): the trace marks each hit on a triangle with the key of its material, the marks of a slice of the cache's tile list are collected, sorted by material (reflectionHardwareRayTracingBucketMaterials) and lit where they stand — the material, the lights and their shadow rays, the sun's shadow ray running as far as screenProbeMaxTraceDistance, the surface cache's indirect light or the sky light's — then the sky light that leaks onto the hit is added where the cache makes irradiance maps and the sum is written to the trace atlas under the cache's pre-exposure. No face is culled in the cache's trace; a hit on the back of a surface that is not two-sided ends the ray with no light, as in the reference. The cache's rays have one bounce, no refraction and no reflection capture whatever reflectionMaxBounces and the other path settings say. The slices are as many tiles as the rays' radiance (64 bytes a ray, the largest of the 80 the lists hold) fits in a storage binding of the device, so a very large update takes more slices and never refuses the mode; the maps held are traced anew when the mode turns on or off.

world.reflections = { hardwareRayTracingLightingMode: 'hitLighting' } // the screen probes' rays and the radiance cache's, lit where they hit
world.indirectLight = { screenProbeRadianceCacheHardwareRayTracing: true } // the cache casts through the scene's triangles (its default)

reflectionMaxBounces (1, from 1 to 64) is the most reflection rays a path of the hit lighting has. With 1 the reflection ray stops at the first lit hit; with more, the path goes on from each lit hit along the reflection of its own specular lobe (a visible normal of the lobe drawn by the frame's noise), weighed by the top layer's reflectance met (the environment BRDF of the specular colour toward the eye), so that a mirror seen in a mirror shows the room and not only the surface cache; each hit of the path is lit as the first (the lights, the sky light, the cache's indirect light) and a ray that leaves the scene reads the sky. The path ends where the roughness it has accumulated is past what the reflections trace (reflectionMaxRoughnessToTrace and its fade), the specular light the next ray does not carry keeping the rough approximation. Each vertex of a path adds 64 bytes a ray to the hit lighting's radiance buffer; where the buffer no longer fits one storage binding of the device the hit lighting is refused with a line in the console naming the bounces and the refraction events (and again when they or the image change).

world.reflections = {
  reflectionHardwareRayTracingHitLighting: true,
  reflectionMaxBounces: 3, // a mirror seen in a mirror, twice
}

reflectionMaxRefractionBounces (0, from 0 to 63) is the refraction events a path of the hit lighting goes through after the first. With 0 the translucent surfaces are passed by, as always; with 1 or more the hit lighting meets them, lights them like any hit, weighed by their coverage, and the path goes on straight through the first surface it met — in the direction it began, from just past that surface — weighed by what the coverage lets through, for up to that many more stretches while any channel of what is left stays at a hundredth or more; each stretch has its own reflections (up to reflectionMaxBounces), and a stretch whose first ray leaves the scene reads the sky and ends the path. reflectionRayTracedTranslucentRefractions (on) is the project's switch: off, the refraction events do nothing. A path holds reflectionMaxBounces × (1 + reflectionMaxRefractionBounces) vertices at most, 64 bytes each in the radiance buffer.

world.reflections = {
  reflectionHardwareRayTracingHitLighting: true,
  reflectionMaxRefractionBounces: 2, // see through two layers of glass
}

Traced translucency

Options of the reflections (packages/sdk-core/src/contracts/tracedTranslucencyOptions.ts), each with the reference's default. translucencyType: 'rayTraced' (or rayTracedTranslucency: 'on') draws the see-through surfaces with rays cast through the scene's triangles, a primary path from the eye through up to translucencyMaxPrimaryHitEvents (4) surfaces and off each a secondary path of up to translucencyMaxSecondaryHitEvents (2) more, ended when its throughput falls under rayTracedTranslucencyPathThroughputThreshold (0.001); translucencyRefraction bends the rays through surfaces of an index of refraction above one (and keeps the rays one a pixel); rayTracedTranslucencyForceOpaque (false) makes the rays treat every surface as opaque: by default a ray passes the holes of a masked material (a surface with an alphaTest, cut where its opacity times its base map's alpha is under the threshold, at the finest level of the map), set, the holes are filled and the rays skip the test; rayTracedTranslucencySampleTranslucentReflectionInReflections (true), rayTracedTranslucencyDownsampleFactor (1) and rayTracedTranslucencyMaxRayIntensity (1000, in the display's white) complete it.

const world = await createWorld({
  reflections: {
    translucencyType: 'rayTraced',
    translucencyRefraction: true,
    translucencyMaxPrimaryHitEvents: 6,
  },
})
world.reflections = { rayTracedTranslucencyMaxRayIntensity: 200 } // changed from the next frame

The traced translucency runs where the scene is traced through its triangles and the image has a transparent front layer: one ray a pixel the layer covers (a block of rayTracedTranslucencyDownsampleFactor pixels a side casting one) is cast from the eye to just short of the opaque depth, the radiance, the throughput and the background it lets show are resolved and accumulated over the images (the reflections' history length and clamp), and the lit image is multiplied by the throughput and the radiance laid over it. The raster draws of the transparents are then left out (particles are still drawn); until the kernels are compiled, or where the image has no front layer, the raster draws them as before. A hit's material is the constants of the surface its placement wears; its light is the surface cache's where the placement has cards, plus the sky light's irradiance on the diffuse colour of a translucent surface.

const g = material.graph('surface')
g.output('baseColor', g.constant(0.05, 0.08, 0.1))
g.output('opacity', g.constant(0)) // pure water; 1 shows the base material alone (foam)
g.output('scatteringCoefficients', g.constant(0.0003, 0.0004, 0.0006)) // per centimetre
g.output('absorptionCoefficients', g.constant(0.0004, 0.00015, 0.0001))
g.output('phaseG', g.constant(0.2))
g.output('colorScaleBehindWater', g.constant(1, 1, 1))
g.output('roughness', g.constant(0.05))
const water = material.meshStandard({ graph: g }) // wired to a water output: drawn as the water

The settings are the reference's r.Water.SingleLayer.*, each an option of createWorld too, held over the quality preset (which writes none of them), changed later from the next frame (packages/sdk-core/src/contracts/singleLayerWaterOptions.ts); a value a setting does not take is refused. Distances are metres, where the reference's are centimetres:

FieldMeaningDefault
singleLayerWaterWhether the water is drawntrue
singleLayerWaterReflectionThe reflection: 'enabled' (the front layer's trace), 'disabled', 'captures' (the captures and the sky) or 'screenSpace' (the screen march and the captures, no scene ray)'enabled'
singleLayerWaterReflectionDownsampleTimes fewer pixels a side (1 or 2) the water's reflections are traced at1
singleLayerWaterReflectionCheckerboardWith a downsample of 2, blocks of two pixels across and one downfalse
singleLayerWaterReflectionReconstructionA pixel rebuilds its reflection from the rays round itfalse
singleLayerWaterReflectionDenoisingThe temporal and the bilateral denoising of the water's reflectionsfalse
singleLayerWaterReflectionTemporalThe temporal denoising of the 'screenSpace' techniquetrue
singleLayerWaterUnderwaterFogWhenCameraIsAboveWaterThe height fog is also laid on the scene seen through the water, at the depth of what lies behind it, with the camera above the waterfalse
singleLayerWaterTiledCompositeThe reflection composite draws the 8 by 8 tiles that hold water, not the whole targettrue
singleLayerWaterTiledSceneColorCopyThe scene's colour is copied for those tiles alone (with the refraction culling on and the copy not downsampled)true
singleLayerWaterWaveOpsThe tiles are listed with subgroup operations where the device grants themtrue
singleLayerWaterDepthPrepassThe water's depth is drawn first (the tiles and the refraction mask need it)true
singleLayerWaterOptimizedClearThe scene's depth is copied over the view alone, not the whole texturetrue
singleLayerWaterVelocityOutputPassWhen the water writes its velocity: 'depthPrepass' (right after its depth), 'basePass' (with its shading) or 'none''depthPrepass'
singleLayerWaterShadersSupportDistanceFieldShadowThe programs keep the sun apart from the rest of the water's light, for the sun's distance-field shadow; read when the session openstrue
singleLayerWaterDistanceFieldShadowThe sun's light on the water is kept apart for the sun's distance-field shadow, which leaves out the meshes made of clusters (all the engine draws; the shadow maps shadow them) (needs the setting above and meshes with fields)true
singleLayerWaterShadersSupportVsmFilteringThe programs hold the full trace of the sun's shadow for the water; read when the session opensfalse
singleLayerWaterVsmFilteringThe sun's shadow on the water is the full projection the opaque surfaces get, not one sample: the shading reads the sun unshadowed (shadowSkipSun), the shadow maps are projected onto the water's surface over the tiles that hold water, and the separated sun is multiplied by that share before the composite (needs the setting above and singleLayerWaterDepthPrepass, which lists the tiles)false
singleLayerWaterCloudShadowThe clouds shade the sun that lights the water's volumefalse
singleLayerWaterRefractionDownsampleTimes fewer pixels a side (1 or 2) the copy of the scene the water refracts is made at1
singleLayerWaterRefractionCullingSkip the refraction where it shows little (the three cullings below)false
singleLayerWaterRefractionDistanceCullingMetres from the camera past which the refraction is skipped; 0 none0
singleLayerWaterRefractionDistanceCullingFadeRangeMetres over which it fades out before that distance4
singleLayerWaterRefractionFresnelCullingFresnel reflectance above which the refraction is skipped; 0 none0
singleLayerWaterRefractionFresnelCullingFadeRangeThe Fresnel range over which it fades out0.2
singleLayerWaterRefractionDepthCullingMetres of water depth below which the refraction is skipped; 0 none0
singleLayerWaterRefractionDepthCullingFadeRangeMetres of depth over which it fades out1

The water writes its velocity as the reference's water pass does: the vectors of the texels it covers become the camera's motion at the water's depth and their visibility identifiers are cleared, so that the temporal pass and the motion blur read a surface that moves with the camera alone. Not ported: ForceVelocity (deprecated, ignored by the reference itself), MobileFallback and r.ParallelSingleLayerWaterPass (a mobile renderer and a render-thread parallelism this engine does not have). screenSpace is the screen march alone — full resolution, no scene ray, no far screen trace, no reconstruction or spatial filter —, captures the captures and the sky, disabled no reflection.

const world = createWorld('viewer', { singleLayerWaterRefractionDownsample: 2 }) // a coarser copy of the scene
world.singleLayerWater = { singleLayerWaterReflection: 'captures' } // no ray: the captures and the sky, from the next frame
world.singleLayerWater = {
  singleLayerWaterRefractionCulling: true,
  singleLayerWaterRefractionDistanceCulling: 200,
}
world.singleLayerWater = { singleLayerWaterReflection: null } // given back its default

The explorer takes the same by field (explorer.setSingleLayerWater('singleLayerWaterReflection', 'captures')), and an agent through trillion3d_set_single_layer_water.

heterogeneous-volumes.title: Heterogeneous volumes: voxel grids and the volumetric shadow map
heterogeneous-volumes.description: Voxel grids and the volumetric shadow map: the settings of the heterogeneous volumes.
heterogeneous-volumes.html:
world.heterogeneousVolumeRendering holds the settings of the heterogeneous volumes. Besides the live shading, the volumes can be shadowed through voxel grids: a grid cut in the view's frustum and an axis-aligned one over the volumes' bounds, each a top level of cells holding bottom-level voxels (heterogeneousVolumesBottomLevelGridResolution, 1 to 4, 4 by default; an indirection grid of heterogeneousVolumesIndirectionGridResolution, 4, while heterogeneousVolumesIndirectionGrid is on). A grid of the greatest extinction of each top-level cell (heterogeneousVolumesMajorantGrid, on; heterogeneousVolumesMajorantGridMax, off, adds the chain down to one cell) and a bitmask of the occupied cells (heterogeneousVolumesTopLevelBitmask, off) speed up the tracking. The shadow of a light or of the camera is then a list of samples a texel (heterogeneousVolumesShadowsMaxSampleCount, 8, kept within heterogeneousVolumesShadowsRelativeErrorThreshold 0.05 and ...AbsoluteErrorThreshold 0, compressed while heterogeneousVolumesShadowsUseAvsmCompression is on). heterogeneousVolumesShadowsPipeline picks the way: 0, the default, shades the volumes live; 1 builds the grids. Sparse voxels (heterogeneousVolumesSparseVoxel, off, with ...GenerationMipBias, ...PerTileCulling and ...Refinement) are the cells of a coarse level where a volume has density.

heterogeneousVolumesShadowsType picks the map the volumes' cast shadows are kept in: 1, the default, the beer map (the first and last place with extinction of each texel and the transmittance at both); 0 the adaptive volumetric shadow map, a list of up to heterogeneousVolumesShadowsMaxSampleCount samples a texel (each volume's list combined with the volumes' before it, then compressed in two levels), read by the lit passes in place of the beer map. A resolution that would not fit the device's storage buffer is halved. heterogeneousVolumesHardwareRayTracing (off), with heterogeneousVolumesPreshading on, makes the march visit only the spans of the sparse voxels a ray meets: the voxels (...SparseVoxelGenerationMipBias, ...SparseVoxelRefinement) are cut out of the baked extinction, a hierarchy of boxes is built over them and each pixel's ray walks it, front to back, by a compute pass.

world.heterogeneousVolumeRendering = {
  heterogeneousVolumesShadows: true,
  heterogeneousVolumesShadowsType: 0, // adaptive volumetric shadow map
  heterogeneousVolumesPreshading: true,
  heterogeneousVolumesHardwareRayTracing: true, // march only the voxels the ray meets
  heterogeneousVolumesSparseVoxelRefinement: true,
}
world.heterogeneousVolumeRendering = {
  heterogeneousVolumesShadows: true,
  heterogeneousVolumesShadowsPipeline: 1,
  heterogeneousVolumesFrustumGridShadingRate: 2, // voxels two pixels wide in the view
  heterogeneousVolumesMinimumVoxelSizeInFrustum: 0.05, // metres
  heterogeneousVolumesShadowsMaxSampleCount: 16,
}

With heterogeneousVolumesShadowsPipeline at 1 the grids are built in the shadows phase of every image, whether or not the volumes cast shadows. The volumes are rasterized into them: each top-level cell a volume's box meets gets the voxel its distance and heterogeneousVolumesShadowsShadingRate (1 pixel in the view, ...ShadowsOutOfFrustumShadingRate 2 out of it) ask, its bottom level and indirection cells are taken from pools sized by heterogeneousVolumesOrthoGridMaxBottomLevelMemoryInMegabytes (128, ...FrustumGridMaxBottomLevelMemoryInMegabytes 128 for the frustum grid, which the shadows do not build), and the volume's material is evaluated at the voxels. A region of a bottom level whose extinction hardly varies (a relative error under heterogeneousVolumesBottomLevelGridHomogeneousAggregationThreshold, 0.001, and under four empty voxels) is stored as one voxel while heterogeneousVolumesBottomLevelGridHomogeneousAggregation is on, the default. A pool that is full leaves the cells that would not fit empty; a bottom level of three voxels a side takes two, which the Morton order the cells are found by needs. heterogeneousVolumesShadowsLightDirectional, ...Point, ...Spot and ...Rect, all on, say which kinds of light cast a volumetric shadow. The map of each light is rendered through the grids, a list of samples a texel along the rays of the light's beer map, and kept as that map, or as the adaptive one with heterogeneousVolumesShadowsType 0.

heterogeneousVolumesDebug (0, off) replaces the image of the volumes by the transmittance through the grids, the opacity left in the alpha and, in the colour, what the way of finding it gathers: 1 walks the ortho grid and the frustum grid cell by cell; 2 to 5 follow the ray by samples (steps of a voxel, the majorant of the cell under each step, the greatest majorant of the grid, the cells of the majorant grid in turn); 6 to 9 track it with random walks (spectral weighted delta, ratio, spectral ratio, the cells of the majorant grid in turn, each by delta tracking), one walk a pixel, so the image is noisy and the temporal pass accumulates it. The views world.diagnostic.mode takes, 'heterogeneous-volumes-dda-marching', '...-sample-marching', '...-sample-majorant', '...-sample-max-majorant', '...-sample-majorant-dda', '...-delta-tracking', '...-ratio-tracking', '...-spectral-ratio-tracking' and '...-tracking-majorant-dda', are the modes 1 to 9.

// The shadows traced through the grids, and the grids seen by the walk of a ray through the majorant grid, cell by cell.
world.heterogeneousVolumeRendering = {
  heterogeneousVolumesShadows: true,
  heterogeneousVolumesShadowsPipeline: 1,
  heterogeneousVolumesOrthoGridMaxBottomLevelMemoryInMegabytes: 256,
  heterogeneousVolumesShadowsLightPoint: false, // only the sun casts a volumetric shadow
  heterogeneousVolumesBottomLevelGridHomogeneousAggregationThreshold: 0.01,
}
world.diagnostic.mode = 'heterogeneous-volumes-sample-majorant-dda'

Reference: world.heterogeneousVolumeRendering.

subsurface-profile.title: The scattering of the light under a surface (subsurface profile)
subsurface-profile.description: Spread a surface's diffuse light beneath it with a subsurface profile: the shading model, the profile fields and the settings.
subsurface-profile.html:
A surface whose material graph picks the subsurface-profile shading model (shadingModel: 'subsurfaceProfile', or a graph's output 5 under fromMaterialExpression) lights as a plain one, then the engine spreads its diffuse light over the neighbouring pixels of the lit image by the profile's scattering, and multiplies the result by the surface's colour: skin, wax, marble. The light is spread in the image, after the lights, the indirect light and the reflections and before the sky, the fog and the transparents; the specular light is not. A profile is a subsurface profile asset (SubsurfaceProfile: the colour and mean free path the light travels, the world unit scale, the boundary colour bleed, the dual specular and the transmission); a pixel keeps its profile's number in the table of profiles the engine holds (setSubsurfaceProfiles), the default skin being profile 0; the material parameter that names a profile is subsurfaceProfile (below). By default a profile is scattered by importance sampling, a few samples a pixel chosen for the pixel's variance and drawn from the profile's own distribution; a profile of implementation: 'separable' is scattered by two separable passes. Each setting has the default of the reference's fourth quality level.

The profile of a material is its subsurfaceProfile parameter: any of the fields of the reference's subsurface profile asset, the others being the default skin's (scatterRadius 1.2, subsurfaceColor, falloffColor, boundaryColorBleed, extinctionScale, scatteringDistribution 0.93, normalScale 0.08, ior 1.55, roughness0 0.75, roughness1 1.3, lobeMix 0.85, surfaceAlbedo, meanFreePathColor, meanFreePathDistance, worldUnitScale, transmissionTintColor, tint, distanceScale, burley, meanFreePath and implementation). A material that names none is scattered by the default skin; two that name the same profile share it (at most 255 profiles).

// Skin: a profile of its own, scattered by the pass, with no graph. `subsurfaceOpacity` (above 0.1) is the share of the profile's
// radius the pixel scatters over.
const skin = material.meshPhysical({
  color: 0xcc8c73,
  roughness: 0.45,
  shadingModel: 'subsurfaceProfile',
  subsurfaceProfile: { scatterRadius: 1.2, lobeMix: 0.85, roughness0: 0.75, roughness1: 1.3 },
  subsurfaceOpacity: 1,
})
// A graph decides each pixel's model only under `shadingModel: 'fromMaterialExpression'`.

The shading model of a material (shadingModel, the reference's own names: defaultLit the default, unlit, subsurface, preintegratedSkin, clearCoat, subsurfaceProfile, twoSidedFoliage, hair, cloth, eye, singleLayerWater, thinTranslucent, toon (the model of material.meshToon, no graph picks it: see below), and fromMaterialExpression, the model the shadingModel output of the material's graph gives each pixel; under any other name the graph's output is ignored, as the reference ignores it). With no graph, as material parameters: unlit shows emissive (times emissiveIntensity, and its map) alone; preintegratedSkin is lit by subsurfaceColor and subsurfaceOpacity; subsurfaceProfile by subsurfaceProfile and subsurfaceOpacity; eye by irisMask (the share that is iris, 1 by default), irisDistance (0.1 by default, the caustic's concavity) and a profile, the iris looking along (0, 0, -1); hair by its fibre direction, the page's tangent (the surface's normal where the mesh stores none), metalness as its scatter amount, and roughness. The clear coat and the cloth are their parameters (clearcoat, clearcoatRoughness, sheen, sheenColor, sheenRoughness), the thin subsurface (subsurface, twoSidedFoliage) the subsurfaceColor of a double-sided surface. singleLayerWater and thinTranslucent stay node-driven, as in the reference: their inputs are the water's and the thin translucent's output nodes of the material's graph.

The toon material (material.meshToon, a standard surface of the toon shading model: color, metalness, roughness, specularIntensity, emissive, the normal map and anisotropy are read as a standard surface's) lights its pixels in bands: the diffuse light goes through the ramp of its toonProfile at the cosine of the normal with the light, remapped from [-1, 1] to [0, 1], and the specular lobe, divided by its peak, through the specular ramp. The profile (toonProfile, any of its fields, the others the default profile's; none: the default profile) holds diffuseRamp and specularRamp (lists of [time, value] keys, a value a grey or [r, g, b], linear between keys: the defaults are four diffuse bands at 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 and a hard specular at the lobe's middle), diffuseRampOffsetTexture / diffuseRampOffsetStrength (0) / diffuseRampOffsetSize (1) and the same three for the specular (an image whose grey level, remapped to [-1, 1], moves the ramp's input over the surface, repeated size times over the fraction of the mesh's first texture coordinates), shadowHatchingPatternTexture (an image whose red, green, blue and alpha channels draw the shadow from light to dark), shadowHatchingPatternDistributionRamp (the shadow in, the weight out, a list of [time, value] keys; the default is the identity), shadowHatchingPatternSize (1) and shadowHatchingPatternStrength (1), shadowExtinctionCoefficient (10, per metre, 0 to 100: how deep light goes into the surface for the shadow maps — the light that survives an occluder distance of d centimetres is exp(-d * shadowExtinctionCoefficient / 100), a value of 1 leaving 36% after a metre), diffuseIndirectScale (1), specularIndirectScale (1, the scale of the reflections), specularIndirectRamp (the keys [time, value] of the ramp that quantises the reflections; the default is the identity) with specularIndirectRampRepetition (0: no quantisation; above 0, how many times the ramp repeats over the range of the reflections' luminance, once the setting toonReflectionQuantization of world.shading is on) and diffuseRampIncludesShadow (false: the shadow multiplies the banded diffuse; true: it multiplies the ramp's input). The offset and hatching images repeat over ten times the fraction of the mesh's first texture coordinates (the repetition the sizes multiply). A profile is held while a material wears it and its row is free again when the material is disposed or declared with another profile: up to 255 distinct profiles at once, 16 of which may wear images.

const toon = material.meshToon({
  color: 0xe0a060,
  roughness: 0.5,
  toonProfile: {
    // Three bands and a bright rim of specular, the middle band tinted.
    diffuseRamp: [[0, 0.1], [0.4, 0.1], [0.41, [0.9, 0.6, 0.5]], [0.7, [0.9, 0.6, 0.5]], [0.71, 1], [1, 1]],
    specularRamp: [[0, 0], [0.8, 0], [0.81, 1], [1, 1]],
    diffuseRampOffsetTexture: halftone, // a Texture whose grey level offsets the bands over the surface
    diffuseRampOffsetStrength: 0.15,
    diffuseRampOffsetSize: 8,
  },
})
SettingMeaningDefault
subsurfaceScatteringThe master switch; off, such a surface is lit as a plain onetrue
subsurfaceScaleA scale on every profile's radius; 0 is off, below 1 narrower, above 1 wider1
subsurfaceHalfResolutionScatter at half the image's size: faster, of lower qualityfalse
subsurfaceHalfResolutionSeparableIn half resolution, scatter every profile with the separable passestrue
subsurfaceRecombineQualityHow the lit image is rebuilt and recombined: 0 low, 1 high, -1 automatic (high); an accumulated image is always high1
subsurfaceFilterThe scattered image is read with the bilinear filter (off: the nearest texel)true
subsurfaceSampleSetThe separable passes' samples a side: 0 is 6, 1 is 9, 2 is 132
subsurfaceCheckerboard0: the lit image's alpha holds the diffuse light's luminance; 1: a checkerboard of diffuse and specular; 2: automatic (0)2
subsurfaceCheckerboardNeighborValidationWith the checkerboard, a neighbour that is not a profile pixel adds nothing to the reconstructionfalse
subsurfaceBurleyQuality0 scatters every profile with the separable passes; 1 the sampled scattering, the separable ones in half resolution1
subsurfaceBurleySamplesA fixed count of samples a pixel for the sampled scattering; 0 lets the pixel's variance choose it0
subsurfaceBurleyProfileIdCacheEach pixel's profile kept in a texture the passes read in place of the surfaces (a byte a pixel)true
subsurfaceBurleyBilateralKernelA sample weighs by depth alone (0) or depth and normal (1)1
subsurfaceBurleyMipsMinTileCountThe count of tiles of sampled scattering from which the diffuse light's mip chain is made; 0 always4000
subsurfaceSubpixelThresholdThe share of the scattering inside the pixel's own footprint above which a tile is not scattered1
subsurfaceSamplingChannelThe channel that steers the sampled scattering: 0 the largest diffuse mean free path, 1 the largest mean free path1
subsurfaceColorTransmittanceDistanceThe distance (0.05 to 1) at which a subsurface material's colour is read as the light's transmittance (its hue shift)0.15

The quality presets write the scale, the separable samples, the recombine's quality and the half resolution: smooth a scale of 0, balanced 0.75, both with the lowest sample set, the low recombine and the half resolution; fine the scale 1, the medium sample set, the automatic recombine and the half resolution; cinematic the defaults at the full resolution; max writes nothing. A view pays its textures only while a resident surface may carry the model: at full resolution about 40 bytes a pixel (the setup texture with its mips, two scattering targets, the history pair, the recombined image and the profile ids).

const world = createWorld('viewer', { subsurfaceScale: 0.5 }) // a narrower scattering
world.subsurfaceScattering = { subsurfaceHalfResolution: true } // from the next frame, at half the size
world.subsurfaceScattering = { subsurfaceBurleySamples: 32 } // a fixed 32 samples a pixel
world.subsurfaceScattering = { subsurfaceColorTransmittanceDistance: 0.3 } // the `subsurface` model's hue shift, weaker
world.subsurfaceScattering = { subsurfaceScale: null } // given back to the preset
world.subsurfaceScattering = { subsurfaceScattering: false } // off: no pass, no texture, no byte

The explorer takes the same by field (explorer.setSubsurfaceScattering('subsurfaceScale', 2)), and an agent through trillion3d_set_subsurface_scattering.

Reference: SubsurfaceProfile, world.shading.

see-through-surface-pass.title: The pass of the image a see-through surface is drawn in
see-through-surface-pass.description: Choose the pass of the image in which a see-through surface is drawn, before or after the depth of field.
see-through-surface-pass.html:
A see-through surface is drawn apart from the scene and laid over the image once the depth of field has read it, so that no blur reaches it (translucencyPass: 'afterDepthOfField', the default). A surface that should be blurred with the scene it lies in — a haze, a distant window — says 'beforeDepthOfField': it is laid onto the scene before the depth of field. A surface that should stay as sharp as it was drawn — a hologram, a HUD element in the world — says 'afterMotionBlur': it is laid over the image after the temporal anti-aliasing and the motion blur have read it, so neither smears it (its edges are not anti-aliased by the temporal pass either). A particle pool takes the same setting in its spec (ParticlePoolSpec.translucencyPass). Without a depth of field on the image the first two passes draw alike; the third is its own pass whatever the image. The scene pays a second set of translucency targets and an image of the display's size only while one of its surfaces or pools names 'afterMotionBlur'.

material.meshStandard({ transparent: true, opacity: 0.3, translucencyPass: 'beforeDepthOfField' }) // blurred with the scene
material.meshStandard({ transparent: true, opacity: 0.5, translucencyPass: 'afterMotionBlur' }) // never smeared by the temporal pass nor the motion blur
new ParticlePool({ capacity: 64, translucencyPass: 'afterMotionBlur' }) // a pool's, in its spec

light-source-radius.title: A lamp's source radius and its housing
light-source-radius.description: A point or spot light's source radius: how soft its shadow is and how the lamp lights a surface.
light-source-radius.html: SceneLight.emitterRadius (metres, positive, below range, point and spot only) is the radius of the source sphere: it sets how soft the light's shadow is and how the lamp lights a surface. A lamp's housing (a lantern glass, a shade) that must not put its own light out is a mesh with mesh.castShadow = false, as any mesh.

spot-light-cone.title: A lamp's cone, fall-off and share of light
spot-light-cone.description: A spot light's inner and outer cone, its fall-off and the share of light each part gets.
spot-light-cone.html:
A spot light's edge is a fade, not a line. Its innerConeAngle is the half-angle, in radians, of the cone where the light is whole; it fades to nothing at its outerConeAngle, by the square of a ramp in the cosine between the two. The inner cone is 0 by default, so the light fades across the whole cone; an inner cone as wide as the outer one makes the edge sharp (the fade is a milliradian wide). The inner cone is held between 0 and 88.9 degrees, the outer one at least a milliradian past it.

light.spot({ outerConeAngle: 0.6, innerConeAngle: 0.3, distance: 20 }) // whole inside 0.3 rad, nothing at 0.6
light.spot({ outerConeAngle: 0.6, innerConeAngle: 0.6 }) // a sharp edge at 0.6 rad

A point or spot light falls off as the inverse square of the distance, a square centimetre longer, windowed to nothing at its distance: that is inverseSquared: true, the default. With inverseSquared: false it falls off by the range alone: its light is one less the square of the distance over the square of distance, to the power radialExponent (8 by default; greater is a tighter pool), and no weight by distance beyond that.

light.point({ distance: 12, inverseSquared: false }) // exponent 8
light.point({ distance: 12, inverseSquared: false, radialExponent: 2 }) // a wide soft pool

Every light, of any kind, takes two shares of what it gives: diffuseShare of its diffuse light (also its light through a thin surface and the light it gives the bounce) and specularShare of its specular light (the highlight), each from 0 to 1, 1 by default. A fill light that must not make highlights is specularShare: 0; a light that must only make a highlight is diffuseShare: 0.

light.rectArea({ width: 2, height: 1, specularShare: 0 })
light.directional({ diffuseShare: 0.5, specularShare: 1 })
OptionApplies toDefaultMeaning
outerConeAnglespot44°Half the outer cone's opening, in radians (44° is 0.7679): the light is nothing at it.
innerConeAnglespot0Half the inner cone's opening, in radians: the light is whole inside it.
inverseSquaredpoint, spottrueFalls off as the inverse square of the distance; false uses radialExponent.
radialExponentpoint, spot8Exponent of the fall-off when inverseSquared is false; above 0.
diffuseShareevery kind1Share of the diffuse light given, 0 to 1.
specularShareevery kind1Share of the specular light given, 0 to 1.

The compiler's lights (lights.json) and a scene file's lights take the defaults. A saved world keeps the options a light sets and nothing for the defaults; a world saved before version 5 keeps the cone it saved, its angle read as the outer cone and its inner cone that angle less its penumbra share.

imported-lights.title: Lights imported from the source file
imported-lights.description: The lights the compiler writes from a source file, and how the world reads them.
imported-lights.html:
The compiler writes a source file's lights beside the manifest as lights.json: glTF from KHR_lights_punctual, FBX through ufbx, USD from the UsdLux sphere, disk, rect and distant schemas, Blender from Lamp blocks; OBJ declares none. Positions and directions are world space, after instancing: a light instanced by three nodes is three entries.

Units. glTF's values (candela for point and spot, lux for directional) are the engine's intensity as they stand: no luminous efficacy divides them, no hidden gain, and the exposure maps the number to the picture. FBX's Intensity, a percentage, converts at 1000 lm / 4π ≈ 79.6 cd for a point or spot and 10 000 lux for a directional. A point or spot without range gets an unbounded one (1e20 m, as glTF defines it: the light reaches every cell of the light grid); a declared range is kept as written, with no ceiling. A spot keeps the innerConeAngle and outerConeAngle the file writes (glTF's defaults, 0 and π/4, where it names none), and a point or spot names its unit, candelas. A light breaking the contract is counted in rejected and left out.

A light casts when the file says so (glTF says nothing, so imported glTF lights cast). Every light is read as (await scene.load(url)).lights in cache order (imported-lights counts them), each a child of the model, changed like any light. A cache without lights.json has none.

memory-budgets.title: Memory budgets
memory-budgets.description: The memory budgets a host sets and reads: geometry and texture pools, their defaults and what happens past them.
memory-budgets.html:
What a host sets and reads.

SettingDefaultWhat it is
world.budget.gpu2 007 MiBevery GPU pool together, divided by world.budget.split
world.budget.cputhe page cache's own defaultwhat the world keeps in CPU memory
world.budget.geometryPool512 MiBslots of a 128 KiB streaming page each, the root pages held beside them in the root region; clamped to geometryPoolCeiling; the call a memory slider makes
world.budget.texturePool512 MiBvirtual-texture tiles, every texture's tail always resident; clamped to texturePoolCeiling; the room the pool grows into, never bytes taken up front
world.budget.canvas3840 × 2160the largest drawing buffer, { width, height }, the effect targets are reserved at
world.budget.physicsDEFAULT_PHYSICS_BUDGETthe physics engine
  • GPU split. The shadow pool, bounce probes and effect targets are reserved first (at their live descriptor bytes), then the geometry and texture pools up to their ceilings; root coverage and texture tails are mandatory, and admission never changes resolution or raises the declared total.
  • GPU total. Unset, it only divides the pools — it grows with what the session holds, so the pools keep their defaults — and refuses nothing: the passes make their targets in the middle of a frame, and no allocation is ever refused for it. Set, it is also the ceiling on what the world allocates (GPU_BUDGET_EXCEEDED below).
  • CPU split. The decoded-page cache takes the whole CPU total (split.pageCache): manifest tables, transfer queue and cut tables (sized by the view and the pool, never the world) are reserved off it, and its entries — pages, decoded baked texture levels and files read whole — share the rest under one budget. A change applies at once, entries leaving by last use, never one a frame keeps.
  • Live textures. A video or a canvas redrawn every frame takes its working texture, textureLiveBytes, from the texture pool; the recorded budget stays the declared one.
  • Canvas. Declared larger, it grows the default total, or takes room from the pools under a page-set total. A canvas drawn past it is never shrunk; the diagnostics say effect targets over budget with the bytes past the reserve.
  • Pools. A read gives what the engine holds; a write is clamped to geometryPoolCeiling / texturePoolCeiling and to what gpu leaves beside the shadows and the other pool, never under the floors (the root cover, the texture tails). On WebGPU geometryAllocationBytes counts the slots and the vertex buffers beside them. Two writes before the next frame settle in one rebalance, the image complete throughout; a budget set during prepare is the later word, its report (durationMs) waiting for prepare. The texture pool's floor, minimum, holds every tail (one tile per texture, 900 a layer) plus one tile to stream into, a layer more when the tails fill whole layers; a shrink never displaces a tail. The pool is made at that floor and grows where a lane runs out of places — its arriving tiles find none —, one layer at a time within the budget (texture-pool-grown), so texturePoolBytes is what is held, not the budget; a growth the device refuses keeps the pool and is asked again after a wait.

The low-level createGpuPageCache pins in tiers: cache.pin(key, 'held') for the root cover, cache.pin(key) for ordinary pins; cache.resize(slots) keeps held pages, then pinned, then unpinned, newest first in each; cache.load(key, signal, 'held') pins a page as it arrives; repinning never lowers a held page; cache.unpin(key) releases both. Its units option names each key's streaming page and offset there ({ unit, offset }): a slot of pageBytes holds one streaming page, its pages packed at their offsets, a victim's slot given up with every page of it; a key it names none of is a streaming page alone. Its roots option ({ slots, bytes }, counted in slots) lays a root region behind the streaming slots: the streaming pages of the rootUrls keys — the root pages — take its grains of bytes, never a streaming slot; cache.resize(slots, grown, roots) lays it anew, the one in place kept when absent, and cache.rootRoom() counts its free grains. GeometryPool.roots is the region the engine draws: it opens at 2048 grains within the scene's root pages and grows as HLOD cells hold theirs.

Coarser, never refused. What a view asks beyond a pool is drawn coarser, by the nearest resident ancestor or a texture tile's coarser level: coverageBudgetLimited and geometryPoolSaturated say so. A value that cannot be held as given is brought to what can, geometryPoolClamp / texturePoolClamp naming why (root-cover, scene, page-cap, minimum, device-limit, ceiling, or null). Only this is refused, by name:

CodeWhen
INVALID_GPU_BUDGET, INVALID_CPU_BUDGET, INVALID_GEOMETRY_POOL_BUDGET, INVALID_TEXTURE_POOL_BUDGETa value that is not a whole number of bytes above zero
INVALID_BUDGET_CANVASa declared canvas that is not a whole number of pixels above zero
GPU_BUDGET_UNDER_MINIMUMa GPU total below the root coverage and texture-tail minima
GPU_BUDGET_UNDER_SHADOW_POOLa GPU total under its fixed shadow share
GEOMETRY_POOL_DEVICE_LIMITa device whose limits cannot hold even the root cover
TEXTURE_POOL_DEVICE_LIMITa device whose limits cannot hold the tails of one texture lane
WEBGPU_GEOMETRY_POOL_REFUSED, WEBGPU_TEXTURE_POOL_REFUSED, WEBGPU_FRAME_TARGETS_REFUSEDthe device refuses a floor or the frame targets
GPU_BUDGET_EXCEEDEDan allocation past a GPU total the page set (or an unknown format): no new image, flush and capture reject; terminal for the session, reopened with enough budget once every session sharing the refused cache is released
SURFACE_DEVICE_LIMITa device dimension limit

out-of-memory.title: Out of memory is absorbed
out-of-memory.description: When the browser refuses an allocation the budget allows, no exception reaches the page: the pool shrinks and the frame goes on coarser.
out-of-memory.html:
The browser may refuse an allocation the budget allows; no exception reaches the page. A refused pool is drawn again at half its bytes, down to its floor, the frame going on coarser; a frame waiting on a shadow pool or frame targets is held, never drawn without its shadows. The gpu-out-of-memory diagnostic names the pool, bytes asked (requestedBytes) and granted (grantedBytes, null when even the floor was refused).

A lost device is recovered without a reload: the session reopens on a new device and rebuilds from the decoded-page cache, fetching nothing it still holds, the canvas keeping its last image. Each session reopen, a recovery included, is said once as session-reopen: cause (device-lost or option, nothing else: no change to the scene's content opens a session again), durationMs (from the loss, for a lost device), framesWithoutImage, keptPages. A mesh, a material, a model with its cells or a world the scene gains joins the running session in place, and one it loses is parked. What the session cannot take in place — a pool or a pass the device refuses, a picture that changed size where the atlas layout is fixed — is said by name, once, as content-refused (kind: 'error', what, reason); the rest of the scene is drawn as it was.

captures-and-image-checks.title: Captures and image checks
captures-and-image-checks.description: Take pixels aside from the view with capture.surface and capture.buffer, to check an image.
captures-and-image-checks.html:
capture.surface(world, { width, height }) and capture.buffer(world, { width, height }) return pixels taken aside from the view. A deterministic image: world.camera.set(pose), await world.awaitPages(), world.render(), then await capture.buffer(...). awaitPages() rejects a requested URL that failed to load (a background load is retried three times at most); it waits for pages, not an image.

A capture draws its view cutViewCaptureDelay images (4 by default; less than 1 reads as 1), the first being the one that finds its cut whole, and reads the last. The temporal antialiasing the world has on runs in the capture from that first image, accumulating them from a history of its own that the capture's view releases with it; under 4 images the last, the one that is read, is drawn without it. One image is drawn without it. The capture shows no motion blur. The main view's history is untouched.

world.cut = { cutViewCaptureDelay: 8 } // eight images, the antialiasing accumulating all of them
const { data } = await capture.buffer(world, { width: 3840, height: 2160 })
world.cut = { cutViewCaptureDelay: 2 } // two images, the last drawn without temporal antialiasing
world.cut = { cutViewCaptureDelay: 1 } // one image, no temporal antialiasing in the capture

gpu-deformation.title: GPU deformation
gpu-deformation.description: Animation clips, mixers and the deformation of a mesh on the GPU: the options that drive them.
gpu-deformation.html:
Imported glTF and FBX clips are model.animations. animation.createMixer(root) binds clips to names below root (a loaded model: its tracks and morph weights); mixer.clipAction(clip) has play(), stop(), seek(seconds) (the pose now, playing or not, kept by a stopped action until a playing one writes over it), weight, timeScale and blendMode; animation.weightsTrack(path, times, values) holds all morph weights at each key; animation.skeleton(bones, inverseBindMatrices?) without matrices uses the current bind pose.

FBX clips are evaluated by ufbx, keys and span kept, curves subdivided to a chord error of 2.5e-7 and Euler steps of 15 degrees at most, so whole turns survive. IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED_ANIMATION refuses skins with unbound vertices or more than 65,536 joints, stepped or extrapolated curves, intermediate shapes, layered or constrained animation, sheared world transforms, more than 36,000 distinct keys and times colliding at float32; a clip is never truncated. Skin weights stay exact float32 source values.

const model = await world.scene.load('/character/cache/native/full/manifest.json')
const mixer = animation.createMixer(model)
const walk = mixer.clipAction(model.animations[0]).play()
walk.weight = 0.8
walk.timeScale = 1.2
// Stop at a repeatable pose, for inspection or a reference comparison.
walk.stop().seek(0.5)
world.invalidate()

A page-created mesh uses mesh.skeleton = animation.skeleton(bones, inverseBindMatrices) with four-component skinIndex / skinWeight attributes; morph targets go in geometry.morphAttributes.position (optionally .normal), then mesh.updateMorphTargets(); node.morphTargetInfluences is animated by animation.weightsTrack or written. Each placement of a shared geometry reads its own palette and weights.

Actions blend by weight; action.blendMode = 'additive' adds the difference from the clip's first key. animation.twoBoneIK(root, mid, end, target, pole?, weight?) solves a bone chain after sampling; animation.windClip(bones, options?) loops bones (direction: [x, z], angle in radians, frequency in Hz). mesh.waves shares the physics' waves with a water mesh.

An instanced skinned object a compile named (objectSettings.skinnedInstance) plays its baked clip on the GPU by itself, from the scene's load: no mixer moves it.

The GPU deforms vertices before culling and drawing. metrics.gpuDeformationMs is the latest measured WebGPU deformation time, null without a timestamp sample.

sampled-lighting-guide-filter.title: Sampled lighting: guide filter
sampled-lighting-guide-filter.description: Join the sets of lights each tile saw with its neighbours' before they guide the next image of the sampled lighting.
sampled-lighting-guide-filter.html:
sampledLightsGuideByHistoryFilter (true) joins the sets of lights each 8-pixel tile saw and did not see with its four neighbours' before they guide the next image of the sampled lighting; it works only while sampledLightsGuideByHistory is on.

// Sampled lighting where each tile guides the draw by its own lights alone.
const world = createWorld('viewer', { sampledLights: true, sampledLightsGuideByHistoryFilter: false })

hair-strands-coverage-mapping.title: Hair strands: coverage mapping
hair-strands-coverage-mapping.description: Take the share of a pixel the strands cover from their count and width, through a coverage table.
hair-strands-coverage-mapping.html:
hairVisibilityCoverageMapping (false) takes the share of a pixel the strands cover from their count and their mean width, mapped through a table of the coverage of that many strands of that width placed at random, instead of the product of what each strand lets through. The strands are counted in a second pass over the ribbons; the tiles with strands and the coverage of their pixels follow the mapped transmittance. It needs hairStrands.

// Strands whose pixel coverage comes from their count and mean width.
const world = createWorld('viewer', { hairStrands: true, hairVisibilityCoverageMapping: true })

path-tracer-and-its-denoiser.title: Path tracer and its denoiser
path-tracer-and-its-denoiser.description: A path-traced render mode of its own: its settings, its samples, and the denoiser that cleans them.
path-tracer-and-its-denoiser.html:
pathTracing (false) draws the view with the path tracer, a render mode of its own that traces the scene's triangles bounce after bounce and adds the samples of each image to those of the one before while the view stands still. The other settings are read only when it is on; each default is the reference's.

SettingDefaultMeaning
pathTracingSamplesPerPixel2048samples each pixel gathers before the image stops accumulating
pathTracingMaxBounces32bounces of a path
pathTracingCompactionDepth6the last bounce whose live paths are packed together (under 1 or past the last bounce: every bounce); the bounces after it go on over the last packed list without packing again, as createScene({ pathTracing: true, pathTracingCompactionDepth: 3 }) does for a scene whose paths mostly end early
pathTracingIndirectDispatchfalsedispatch each packed bounce over exactly the live paths (the same image; a matter of speed)
pathTracingDispatchSize2048side in pixels of the tiles the image is traced in
pathTracingExperimentalfalserarely used modes; adaptive sampling needs it
pathTracingAdaptiveSamplingfalsestop tracing pixels whose error is under the threshold
pathTracingAdaptiveSamplingErrorThreshold0.001that error
pathTracingAdaptiveSamplingVisualize01 active pixels, 2 sample counts, 3 to 7 error mip levels
pathTracingProgressDisplaytruebar of the samples gathered
pathTracingWiperModefalsepath tracer drawn right of the cursor only
pathTracingDenoisertruedenoise at the last sample
pathTracingDenoiserNormalSpace00 world, 1 camera-space normals for the denoiser
pathTracingSpatialDenoisertruethe denoiser's spatial stage (edge-aware, guided by albedo, normals and variance)
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserfalsethe temporal stage, which needs an earlier denoised image
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserMode10 and 1 at the last sample, 2 at every image
pathTracingDenoiserVarianceType1prepass variance: 0 per colour channel, 1 luminance, albedo and normal length
pathTracingDenoiserOutputVarianceTexturefalsealways write the variance image
pathTracingDenoiserRankedLuminanceVariancefalserank the channels before taking the luminance for the variance
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserVisualizeMotionVectorfalsedraw the motion found over the image
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserSubPixelOffsettruerefine the motion under a pixel
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserKappa-1fall-off of the history weight (-1 from DeltaE)
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserEta1error under which the history keeps its full weight (-1 one just-noticeable difference)
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserDeltaE5colour difference at which the history weight reaches zero
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserDeltaEHighFrequency2.1per-pixel colour difference from which the history is cut
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserAlpha1weight of the history in the average
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserSource0motion estimated on 0 denoised radiance, 1 normals, 2 albedo, 3 raw radiance, else a fusion of variances
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserSubPixelOffsetStartMip8coarsest pyramid level with a sub-pixel estimate
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserMotionOperation11 subtracts the motion of the image against itself
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserVisualizeWarp01 the warped history, 2 with the weights
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserDistanceMetrics20 luminance, 1 colour distance, 2 CIE 2000 difference
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserTotalVariationtrueless history where the error varies a lot
pathTracingTemporalDenoiserPatchCount1patches merged in the temporal blend (1 to 16)
pathTracingVisualize'none'draws a field of what each pixel sees in place of the lit image, one sample and no denoiser: Radiance (emission), WorldNormal, WorldSmoothNormal, WorldGeoNormal, WorldTangent, BaseColor, DiffuseColor, SpecularColor, TransparencyColor, TransparencyCount (translucent surfaces the ray goes through), Metallic, Specular, Roughness, Anisotropy, IOR, ShadingModel, LightingChannelMask, WorldPosition, LightGridCount, LightGridAxis, LightGridListHash, LightGridSingular, VolumeLightCount, HitKind, SSSColor, SSSRadius, SSSWeight, SSSPhase, FuzzColor, FuzzRoughness, FuzzAmount, BSDFOpacity, BackfacingNormal, TriangleID, InstanceID, ClusterID; PrimaryRays is the path tracer itself with no air or cloud, denoiser or adaptive sampling; 'none' the lit image. The views see every surface the ray goes through and add their colours in proportion to what they cover
pathTracingVisualizeIncludeTranslucenttruethe views see the meshes that are translucent whole; false, the rays go through them
pathTracingVisualizeSamplesPerPixel1samples the PrimaryRays view gathers (the other views take one)
pathTracingVisualizeMaxCount16lights taken as the red end of the ramp of the views that turn a count into a colour (past it, pink)
pathTracingVisualizeAmbientOcclusionMaxDistance2metres the occlusion ray goes that shades the views of the payload; negative shades by the facing ratio
pathTracingMISMode20 material samples alone, 1 light samples alone, 2 both weighed against each other
pathTracingMISCompensationtruethe sky's importance sampling leaves out what the material's samples find (needs mode 2)
pathTracingMaxPathIntensity24brightest a path off the camera's ray adds (1 to 65504)
pathTracingApproximateCausticstrueroughen the paths that would make caustic speckles
pathTracingEnableEmissivetrueemissive surfaces light the scene
pathTracingBackgroundAlpha0alpha of a pixel that meets nothing
pathTracingSamplerType00 a sequence for each pixel, 1 one sequence across the image
pathTracingFrameIndependentTemporalSeedtruethe random sequence goes on across restarts
pathTracingSkylightCachingtruekeep the sky's sampling tables between images
pathTracingFilterWidth3width of the anti-aliasing filter of the camera's rays (0 to 64); 3 is a Gaussian of half a pixel
pathTracingVisibleLights00 no light seen by the camera, 1 all, 2 the sky alone
pathTracingLightGridResolution256side of the light culling grid (rounded up to a power of two)
pathTracingLightGridMaxCount128most lights a cell keeps (1 to 256)
pathTracingLightGridAxis-1axis the lights are projected along, -1 the best
pathTracingEnableReferenceAtmosphere-11 the paths trace the air as a volume, 0 the sky light stands for it, -1 the view's post process setting (off where it sets none)
pathTracingAtmosphereOpticalDepthLUTResolution512side of the optical depth table the traced air reads its transmittance from (held to what the device makes a texture of)
pathTracingAtmosphereOpticalDepthLUTNumSamples16384samples integrated for each texel of that table
pathTracingEnableAtmosphereGroundfalsethe camera's rays see the planet's ground under the traced air (paths that scattered in it always do)
pathTracingUseAnalyticTransmittancetruetransmittance read from the table; false estimated by stepping through the volume
pathTracingMaxRaymarchSteps768most steps a ray takes through a volume
