pathTracingVolumeMISMode1how lamps and rectangles light a volume (the traced air and the clouds): 0 by the scattering events the density gives; 1 by a point drawn on the ray's stretch of the volume with a density that follows the light's reach (equi-angular sampling), the events then lighting by the suns and the sky alone
pathTracingEnableReferenceCloudstruethe paths march the cloud layer's material as a volume (needs the traced air and a sky with a clouds part); false leaves the clouds to the sky light
pathTracingCloudAccelerationMapResolution512side of the map that bounds the march through the clouds: for each column of the layer, its densest cloud and the heights it was found at (1 to 4096)
pathTracingCloudAccelerationMapNumSamples64samples of the cloud material each image adds to each texel of that map (1 to 65536)
pathTracingCloudAccelerationMapVisualizefalsedraw the map in place of the clouds, to judge its resolution
pathTracingCloudMultipleScatterMode10 none: the material's approximation of multiple scattering is ignored and the roughness cutoff applies; 1 the material's approximation, the cutoff applying; 2 by the paths alone, the cutoff lifted
pathTracingCloudRoughnessCutoff0.05roughness of a path beyond which the clouds are not marched (0 to 1)

Current limits: a hit's material is read back from the lit image where the surface shows, else from the surface cache's cards; there are no glass, subsurface, cloth or hair lobes, no capsule lights, light profiles, light functions or rectangle light textures; the spatial stage is the engine's own edge-aware filter (the reference's is an external neural plug-in, not shipped).

// A path-traced view of 256 samples, 8 bounces, adaptive sampling on.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  pathTracing: true,
  pathTracingSamplesPerPixel: 256,
  pathTracingMaxBounces: 8,
  pathTracingExperimental: true,
  pathTracingAdaptiveSampling: true,
  // Sample the lights alone (no material samples), the camera seeing every light.
  pathTracingMISMode: 1,
  pathTracingVisibleLights: 1,
})
// The light grid's cells drawn on the first surface of every pixel, coloured by their lights up to 8.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  pathTracing: true,
  pathTracingVisualize: 'LightGridCount',
  pathTracingVisualizeMaxCount: 8,
  pathTracingVisualizeAmbientOcclusionMaxDistance: 1,
})
// The count of translucent surfaces each ray goes through, with the meshes that are translucent whole seen, then the path tracer's own primary rays gathering 4 samples.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  pathTracing: true,
  pathTracingVisualize: 'TransparencyCount',
  pathTracingVisualizeIncludeTranslucent: true,
})
const primary = createWorld('viewer', {
  pathTracing: true,
  pathTracingVisualize: 'PrimaryRays',
  pathTracingVisualizeSamplesPerPixel: 4,
})
// The temporal denoiser at every image, history cut sooner, the motion drawn.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  pathTracing: true,
  pathTracingTemporalDenoiser: true,
  pathTracingTemporalDenoiserMode: 2,
  pathTracingTemporalDenoiserDeltaE: 2,
  pathTracingTemporalDenoiserVisualizeMotionVector: true,
})
// The air traced as a volume: the paths scatter in it, the planet's ground visible to the camera.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  pathTracing: true,
  pathTracingEnableReferenceAtmosphere: 1,
  pathTracingEnableAtmosphereGround: true,
  pathTracingAtmosphereOpticalDepthLUTResolution: 256,
  pathTracingUseAnalyticTransmittance: false,
})
// The lamps lighting the traced air by the density's events alone, no point drawn on the ray toward them.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  pathTracing: true,
  pathTracingEnableReferenceAtmosphere: 1,
  pathTracingVolumeMISMode: 0,
})
// The clouds of the sky marched by the paths: a finer map, more samples of the material per image, the material's own approximation of multiple scattering, clouds seen down to rough paths.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  pathTracing: true,
  pathTracingEnableReferenceAtmosphere: 1,
  pathTracingEnableReferenceClouds: true,
  pathTracingCloudAccelerationMapResolution: 1024,
  pathTracingCloudAccelerationMapNumSamples: 128,
  pathTracingCloudMultipleScatterMode: 1,
  pathTracingCloudRoughnessCutoff: 0.2,
})
// The map that bounds the cloud march drawn in place of the clouds, to judge its resolution.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  pathTracing: true,
  pathTracingEnableReferenceAtmosphere: 1,
  pathTracingCloudAccelerationMapVisualize: true,
})

heterogeneous-volumes-preshading.title: Heterogeneous volumes: preshading and level of detail
heterogeneous-volumes-preshading.description: Bake a volume's material into three 3D textures before the march, and the level of detail that follows.
heterogeneous-volumes-preshading.html:
heterogeneousVolumesPreshading (false) bakes a volume's material into three 3D textures (extinction, albedo, emission) before the march, which then reads the textures instead of evaluating the material at each step. heterogeneousVolumesCLOD (true) makes a volume far from the view coarser: its lighting cache, occlusion and baked grid have fewer voxels and its march steps are longer.

SettingDefaultMeaning
heterogeneousVolumesPreshadingMipLevel0level of the baked textures the march reads; the levels are filtered from the first, which the reference never does
heterogeneousVolumesPreshadingPixelFormat20 keeps the red channel alone, 1 to 3 the colour channels
heterogeneousVolumesPreshadingCLOD1baked grid size: 0 the volume's, 1 over the level of detail's factor, 2 the lighting cache's
heterogeneousVolumesCLODBias0above 0 coarser, below 0 sharper
heterogeneousVolumesVolumeResolutionX / Y / Z0above 0, replaces that axis of the resolution the bake, the lighting cache and the occlusion use
heterogeneousVolumesAmbientOcclusionRayCountX / Y4occlusion rays a side, 1 to 8
 
// Baked volumes, sharper than the default level of detail, lit at 64 voxels on every axis.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  heterogeneousVolumesPreshading: true,
  heterogeneousVolumesCLODBias: -1,
  heterogeneousVolumesVolumeResolutionX: 64,
  heterogeneousVolumesVolumeResolutionY: 64,
  heterogeneousVolumesVolumeResolutionZ: 64,
})

hair-strands-compute-raster.title: Hair strands: compute raster
hair-strands-compute-raster.description: Raster the strands' visibility samples in compute instead of the device's rasterizer.
hair-strands-compute-raster.html:
hairVisibilityComputeRaster (false) makes a compute raster write the samples of the strands' visibility in place of the device's rasterizer. It bins the segments of the strands into tiles of the image, then draws each tile with a group of threads. The furthest opaque depth of each tile is found first, so that a segment behind every opaque pixel of a tile is not binned into it. The other settings choose how the segments reach their pixels; each default is the reference's.

SettingDefaultMeaning
hairVisibilityNaiveRasterfalsedraw the segments a thread a segment, the ribbons that span more than a tile shared by a group of threads, instead of binning them
hairVisibilityTileCompactionfalsemerge the partly filled tiles the binners made in the same cell into full tiles before they are drawn
hairVisibilityClassificationfalsesort the segments first: the small ones go to the tiles (or to the naive raster), the larger ones are drawn a thread a segment
hairVisibilityComputeRasterTileSize32side in pixels of a tile, from 8 to 32, rounded down to a power of two
hairVisibilityComputeRasterNumBinners32workgroups that bin the segments (1 to 256)
hairVisibilityComputeRasterNumRasterizers256workgroups that draw the tiles (1 to 1024)
hairVisibilityComputeRasterNumRasterizersNaive256workgroups of the naive raster (1 to 1024)
hairVisibilityNumClassifiers32workgroups of the classification (1 to 256)
hairVisibilityComputeRasterMaxTiles65536most tiles kept, from 1024 to 262144; a tile holds 256 segments, and a device whose storage binding holds fewer tiles takes the most it holds; segments past them are not drawn
 
// Strands drawn by the compute raster, its tiles compacted and its segments classified.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  hairStrands: true,
  hairVisibilityComputeRaster: true,
  hairVisibilityTileCompaction: true,
  hairVisibilityClassification: true,
})

hair-strands-velocity.title: Hair strands: velocity
hair-strands-velocity.description: Choose which sample's velocity a pixel of strands writes: the closest, the average or the largest.
hair-strands-velocity.html:
hairVelocityType ('closest') picks the velocity a pixel of strands writes over the surface's, from the velocity of the strands' samples in that pixel: 'closest' the nearest sample's, 'average' their mean, 'max' the largest. hairVisibilityWriteVelocityCoverageThreshold (0, from 0 to 1) is the share of the pixel the strands must cover to write one; at 0 every pixel with strands does. hairVelocityThreshold (1, from 0 to 512) is the velocity, in the reference's pixel unit (the screen's -1 to 1 span over twice the larger side of the image), above which any sample of a pixel marks it to be resolved at once by the temporal pass: its history restarts, the pixel is sharper and noisier and does not smear.

// Strands that write the mean velocity of their samples, only where they cover half a pixel, and resolve at once from a velocity of 3.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  hairStrands: true,
  hairVelocityType: 'average',
  hairVisibilityWriteVelocityCoverageThreshold: 0.5,
  hairVelocityThreshold: 3,
})

The surfaces the strands cover wholly are in the lighting channels of those strands (the union of the channels of the pixel's samples), so a pass that reads a surface's channels finds the strands'.

hair-strands-curve-raster.title: Hair strands: curve raster
hair-strands-curve-raster.description: The experimental curve raster pipeline: curves, clusters and the options that run it.
hair-strands-curve-raster.html:
renderCurve (false, experimental) runs the curve raster pipeline over the strands. The strands are cut into curves of at most 16 points, grouped by position into clusters of 64 curves; each image the pipeline keeps the instances and clusters that lie in the view and in front of the scene's depth (a furthest-depth pyramid of the scene), counts the visible clusters, cuts their curves into segments that it bins into tiles of 32 pixels by the depth of the scene in each tile (renderCurveRasterNumBinners, 32, from 1 to 256, binners each with counts of their own), and compacts the segments of each tile into depth slices, at most 16 groups of 1024 segments, with a piece of raster work per tile. The device has no mesh shader, so only the software path exists: renderCurveSwRaster (true) runs it, and with it off nothing runs. The raster that draws the compacted segments is not there yet, so the pipeline draws nothing for now. renderCurveRasterNumRasterizers (256, from 1 to 1024) and renderCurveRasterMinCoverage (0.05, from 0 to 1, the coverage under which a raster step stops) are for that raster. Images wider than 8192 pixels skip the pipeline.

// The curve raster with sixteen binners, on its software path.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  hairStrands: true,
  renderCurve: true,
  renderCurveSwRaster: true,
  renderCurveRasterNumBinners: 16,
})

hair-strands-forward-raster.title: Hair strands: forward raster
hair-strands-forward-raster.description: Draw the strands without a visibility buffer.
hair-strands-forward-raster.html:
hairVisibilityComputeRasterForward (false) draws the strands without a visibility buffer. Every control point of the strands in view becomes a sample that is lit once (the material and the lights of the strands run over the points, not over the pixels), then a tiled compute raster shades the segments between the points straight into the image: the segments are cut to the view, binned in tiles of 32 pixels (only the tiles in front of the opaque depth), gathered and ordered by depth, and each tile of 8 pixels takes them front to back, mixing the colours of the lit points along each segment and stopping when its pixels are covered. It takes the place of hairVisibilityComputeRaster when both are on, keeps no sample a pixel (hairVisibilitySamplesPerPixel, hairVisibilitySortByDepth, hairVisibilityCoverageMapping do not apply) and needs hairStrands. The strands keep the surfaces' velocity, and a point off the image is lit as the nearest pixel of the edge. Its groups are the compute raster's own settings:

SettingDefaultMeaning
hairVisibilityComputeRasterNumBinners32workgroups that bin the segments into tiles, 1 to 256
hairVisibilityComputeRasterNumRasterizers256workgroups that shade the tiles, 1 to 1024
hairVisibilityComputeRasterMaxTiles65536lists of 1024 segments kept, 1024 to 262144; a device whose storage binding holds fewer takes the most it holds, and the segments past them are not drawn
 
// Strands drawn by the forward raster, with fewer, larger groups for a small image.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  hairStrands: true,
  hairVisibilityComputeRasterForward: true,
  hairVisibilityComputeRasterNumBinners: 16,
  hairVisibilityComputeRasterNumRasterizers: 128,
})

hair-strands-g-buffer-write.title: Hair strands: G-buffer write
hair-strands-g-buffer-write.description: Write the strands into the surfaces for the passes that read them next.
hair-strands-g-buffer-write.html:
hairWriteGBufferData (1, from 0 to 3) writes the strands into the surfaces once they are laid on the image, for the passes that read the surfaces next (the reflections and the occlusion of the following image, the passes that tell hair pixels apart). 0 writes nothing; 1 a placeholder: the tangent (0, 0, 1) as the normal, no roughness and the hair shading model, no colour; 2 the mean tangent of the pixel's strand samples as the normal and their mean roughness; 3 the whole surface, the mean base colour too, and takes the opaque depth to the nearest strand's. A pixel written is of the hair shading model, which has no specular lobe, so no reflection is traced for it. The strands' specular and backlit share stay in their samples: the surfaces hold no place for them. It needs hairStrands.

// Strands that write their normal, roughness and colour into the surfaces and their depth into the opaque depth.
const world = createWorld('viewer', { hairStrands: true, hairWriteGBufferData: 3 })

surface-cache-debug-views.title: Surface cache: debug views
surface-cache-debug-views.description: The surface cache's own tables and boxes drawn over the image, as a diagnostic mode or as a setting.
surface-cache-debug-views.html:
The surface cache draws its own tables and boxes over the image, as a diagnostic mode or as a setting (world.surfaceCache); a mode shows its view whatever the setting says, and keeps the cache up while it is shown. Nothing is drawn, and nothing is copied from the GPU, while none is asked.

ModeSettingDefaultWhat it shows
surface-cache-direct-statssurfaceCacheLightingStats: 10the table of the direct light update, from a tenth of the image's width and height: the tiles of each of the 16 priority buckets (eight a line), MaxBucket and MaxTilesFromMaxBucket (the bucket the budget ends in and the tiles of it that fit), then the pages and the tiles the image lights; read back from the GPU a few images late
surface-cache-indirect-statssurfaceCacheLightingStats: 20the same table for the indirect light (radiosity) update
surface-cache-direct-lighting-statssurfaceCacheLightingStats: 30the lights the direct update gathers (#Lights, Batched Lights, Standalone Lights, whether rectangles, light functions and IES lights are among them), the atlas (AtlasResolution, UpdateAtlasSize, MaxUpdateTiles, UpdateFactor), the trace (Method, RT Traces: the groups of 64 shadow traces, an overestimate) and the cards and tiles being updated; read back a few images late
surface-cache-scene-statssurfaceCacheSceneStatsfalseNumPrimitiveGroups, NumMeshCards and NumCards: the placements that have cards, their mesh cards and the cards in the scene
surface-cache-primitive-groupssurfaceCacheVisualizePrimitiveGroupsfalsethe box of every placement that has mesh cards, in white, in the world (the first thirteen hundred: a view's line list holds 16384 segments)

The screen probes and the world's probes have tables of their own, drawn the same way (the numbers come back from the GPU a few images late, and nothing is copied while none is asked):

ModeSettingDefaultWhat it shows
radiance-cache-statsscreenProbeRadianceCacheStatsfalsethe update of the world's probes: MaxProbesInAtlas and ProbesInAtlas (the probes the atlas holds out of the most it can), Unfilled (holding nothing yet), Refreshing (not traced since the lights last changed), Refused (marks refused for want of a probe), Traced Probes (queued by the last pass) and Marked (cells marked)
screen-probe-gather-debugscreenProbeGatherDebugfalseat four fifths of the image's width: NumScreenProbes, NumUniformScreenProbes and NumAdaptiveScreenProbes
screen-probe-tile-statsscreenProbeTileDebugModefalsethe integration's tiles: the tile grid, then the tiles of the Simple, ImportanceSample and All modes and their total, with the legend in green, orange and cyan, and each tile of the three modes filled half transparent in its colour over the pixels it covers (needs screenProbeIntegrationTileClassification)
screen-probe-placementscreenProbeGatherDebugProbePlacement0where the screen probes stand: 1 a 2-pixel quad at the pixel of every probe (yellow uniform, magenta adaptive), 2 the adaptive probes alone, 3 a cross of 2 cm and a 10 cm line along the normal at each probe's point; drawn by the GPU through one buffer of up to 262144 appended lines, nothing allocated while none is asked (the mode shows 1)
screen-probe-tracesscreenProbeGatherVisualizeTracesfalsethe rays of the screen probe nearest to the cursor (to the middle of the image where none is set): a line from the probe along each ray, as long as the distance it reached, coloured by the radiance it brought back seen through the table the image is composed with (the colour grade and the display curve at the image's exposure); a ray that ended within 1 cm of its probe is drawn red and 5 cm long. screenProbeGatherVisualizeTracesFreeze (false) keeps the rays as they were at the last image that updated them so the camera can move round them; visualizeUseShaderPrintForTraces (true) set to false draws the lines against the opaque depth, a ray behind a surface hidden by it, and always through the composition's table; visualizeToneMap (true) set to false colours the lines drawn over everything by the display's transfer alone; debugCursorX and debugCursorY (-1, none) set the cursor in display pixels
reflection-tracesreflectionVisualizeTracesfalsethe reflection ray of the pixel under the cursor (debugCursorX, debugCursorY; nothing where none is set): a line from the surface along the ray, as long as the distance it reached, in the radiance it brought back as it is, a yellow cross of 2 cm at its end, and the grid texel, the distance and the radiance as text, read back from the GPU a few images late; needs the reflections to have traced an image
radiance-cache-probesradianceCacheVisualize0a sphere at every probe of the world's probes, hidden by the surfaces in front of it: coloured by the irradiance it holds along its surface at an albedo of 0.3 (a probe inside a surface red, one moved off the surfaces tinted green, an adaptive one cyan) where the irradiance field is the indirect light, by its radiance otherwise; radianceCacheVisualize: 2 colours it by the share of its rays that left the scene; radianceCacheVisualizeRadiusScale (1) scales the spheres (5% of the cell at one); radianceCacheVisualizeClipmapIndex (-1, all) draws one level, the finest 0
scene-visualizationnone (the mode only)-the scene traced from the camera pixel by pixel through the global distance field, lit by what the surface cache holds at the hit and by the sky where the ray leaves the scene, replacing the image; visualizeSceneTraceRadianceCache (false) ends the trace where the world's probes cover the eye and reads their light past it (their spheres' light, interpolated between the eight probes round the eye), and marks the probes round the eye so that they exist; visualizeHiResSurface (true) reads the finest page of the cache; visualizeMinTraceDistance (0, read as 0.01 at least) and visualizeMaxTraceDistance (100000) bound the trace in centimetres; visualizeToneMap (true) picks the colour curve. visualizeMode (0) shows the scene view by itself with the number of one of its modes (3 the scene, which the diagnostic mode shows; 1 the overview of the geometry normals, the reflection view and the coverage in three labelled tiles; 4 the reflection view, traced as far as the reflections trace; 5 the coverage, pink where a mesh has cards but none covers the point and yellow where it has none; 6 the geometry normals; 8 the albedo; 9 the normals; 10 the emission; 11 the card weights; 12 the direct light; 13 the indirect light; 16 and 17 the images since each page's direct and indirect light were updated; 18 and 19 the last use of the pages; 20 the number of lights each tile tracks the shadow factor of; 21 the sharing of the cards; 24 the radiosity images accumulated); under an orthographic camera every ray runs along the view's direction from its own pixel, and the height fog (reflectionHeightFog, reflectionMinDistanceForFoggingSky) is laid over the light. visualizeSurfaceCacheFeedback (false) lets the view write the cache's feedback so that the modes 18 and 19 show the last use of the pages

The scene table also writes AddOps and RemoveOps: the count of the placements that wanted mesh cards or lost them in the image, then the ids of the first seven.

// The world's probes update table, and the count of the screen probes.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  screenProbes: 'high',
  screenProbeRadianceCacheStats: true,
  screenProbeGatherDebug: true,
})
world.diagnostic.mode = 'screen-probe-tile-stats' // or by mode: the integration's tiles

Reference: world.surfaceCache.

reflections-that-read-the-radiance-cache.title: Reflections that read the radiance cache
reflections-that-read-the-radiance-cache.description: Make the rough reflections read the screen probes' radiance cache instead of tracing their whole ray.
reflections-that-read-the-radiance-cache.html:
reflectionRadianceCache (false) makes the rough reflections read the screen probes' radiance cache (screenProbeRadianceCache, on by default) instead of tracing their whole ray. A pixel whose roughness, plus a blue noise reflectionRadianceCacheRoughnessFadeLength wide (0.05), passes reflectionRadianceCacheMinRoughness (0.2), and whose point the cache covers with all eight probes round it, casts a ray shortened from reflectionRadianceCacheMaxTraceDistance (5000 cm) at that roughness to reflectionRadianceCacheMinTraceDistance (1000 cm) at reflectionRadianceCacheMaxRoughness (0.35), never under the distance the cache asks to be traced before it is read, never over the view's longest ray. A shortened ray that meets nothing within its distance takes the light the cache holds along it from its point, through the cone of its angle, with the sky light's leaking, the height fog and the ceiling of a ray; the far screen trace of the opaque rays is off while the cache is read. reflectionRadianceCacheStochasticInterpolation (true) reads one probe of the eight, drawn by the interpolation weights at one half, false the eight weighed; reflectionRadianceCacheReprojectionRadiusScale (10, from 1 to 100000) scales the sphere round each probe the direction is corrected through. Run-time settings, read again at each image; nothing is traced differently where the cache is not made (the setting off, the probes cast none, the program still compiling).

const world = createWorld('viewer')
world.reflections = { reflectionRadianceCache: true } // rough reflections read the cache past a short ray
world.reflections = { reflectionRadianceCacheMaxTraceDistance: 2000, reflectionRadianceCacheMinTraceDistance: 500 } // shorter rays, centimetres
world.reflections = { reflectionRadianceCacheStochasticInterpolation: false } // the eight probes, weighed
world.reflections = { reflectionRadianceCache: null } // back to the default, off

short-range-occlusion-triangles.title: Short-range occlusion through the scene's triangles
short-range-occlusion-triangles.description: Cast the screen probes' short-range occlusion through the scene's triangles instead of the horizon search.
short-range-occlusion-triangles.html:
screenProbeShortRangeAOHardwareRayTracing (false) casts the screen probes' short-range occlusion, and its bent normal, through the scene's triangles in place of the horizon search or the screen's rays, where the scene has acceleration structures and the program is compiled: a pixel casts four rays (eight from a screenProbeQuality of 2, sixteen from 6), cosine distributed over its hemisphere, from its point moved screenProbeShortRangeAOHardwareRayTracingNormalBias metres (0.001) along its normal, as far as two tiles of pixels of the image's width at its depth; the first hit of an opaque surface blocks a ray, and the amount is the share left open. The short-range global illumination (screenProbeShortRangeGI) is not gathered while it runs. Run-time settings.

const world = createWorld('viewer')
world.indirectLight = { screenProbeShortRangeAOHardwareRayTracing: true } // contact shadows from the scene's triangles
world.indirectLight = { screenProbeShortRangeAOHardwareRayTracingNormalBias: 0.002 } // start the rays 2 mm off the surface
world.indirectLight = { screenProbeShortRangeAOHardwareRayTracing: null } // back to the horizon search
// The reflection ray of the pixel under the point (640, 360) of the display.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  reflectionVisualizeTraces: true,
  debugCursorX: 640,
  debugCursorY: 360,
})
// The spheres at the probes of the finest level of the world's probes, twice their usual size.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  radianceCacheVisualize: 1,
  radianceCacheVisualizeRadiusScale: 2,
  radianceCacheVisualizeClipmapIndex: 0,
})
// The scene traced from the camera, the far field read from the world's probes.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  visualizeSceneTraceRadianceCache: true,
  visualizeMaxTraceDistance: 20000,
})
world.diagnostic.mode = 'scene-visualization'
// The overview of the scene view: the geometry normals, the reflection view and the coverage, side by side (8 would show the albedo alone).
const world = createWorld('viewer', { visualizeMode: 1 })
// The rays of the screen probe under the cursor, drawn against the depth (hidden behind surfaces), in the radiance through the display's table.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  screenProbes: 'high',
  screenProbeGatherVisualizeTraces: true,
  visualizeUseShaderPrintForTraces: false,
  debugCursorX: 640,
  debugCursorY: 360,
})
// The rays of the screen probe under the point (640, 360) of the display, frozen as they are now.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  screenProbes: 'high',
  screenProbeGatherVisualizeTraces: true,
  screenProbeGatherVisualizeTracesFreeze: true,
  debugCursorX: 640,
  debugCursorY: 360,
})
// The direct light's update table, and the boxes of the placements that have cards.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  surfaceCache: { surfaceCacheLightingStats: 1, surfaceCacheVisualizePrimitiveGroups: true },
})
world.diagnostic.mode = 'surface-cache-scene-stats' // or by mode: the counts of the scene

reservoir-gather-of-the-indirect-light.title: Reservoir gather of the indirect light
reservoir-gather-of-the-indirect-light.description: Gather the indirect light of the opaque surfaces by reservoirs instead of screen probes.
reservoir-gather-of-the-indirect-light.html:
finalGatherMethod: 'reservoirs' gathers the indirect light of the opaque surfaces by reservoirs instead of screen probes. One ray a tile of pixels (reservoirGatherDownsampleFactor, 2 by default) is cast through the scene's triangles in a uniform direction of the hemisphere and lit by the surface cache where it hits; its hit is kept in a reservoir, merged with the reservoirs of the last image round where the surface stood (reservoirGatherTemporalResampling), then with those round it in space (reservoirGatherSpatialResampling, reservoirGatherSpatialResamplingNumPasses passes of reservoirGatherSpatialResamplingNumSamples neighbours), upsampled to the pixels (reservoirGatherUpsampleMethod: 'spiral', 'jitteredBilinear' or 'passthrough'), accumulated over the images (reservoirGatherTemporal, reservoirGatherTemporalMaxFramesAccumulated) and blurred where it is still noisy (reservoirGatherBilateralFilter). It needs the scene traces (screenProbeSceneTraces with screenProbeHardwareRayTracing, both on by default); without them the screen probes gather, as they do when the level casts no probes. The rays walk the scene's triangles in a compute stage whatever the device's hardware, so the choice costs what that walk costs. A short-range, full-resolution occlusion (the contact shadows the spatial filtering lacks) is added to the gathered light (reservoirGatherShortRangeAO, on by default; its reach is reservoirGatherShortRangeAOMaxScreenTraceFraction of the screen width, 0.02 by default). It is the screen probes' occlusion pass, so it follows their switch (screenProbeShortRangeOcclusion), reduction (screenProbeShortRangeAODownsampleFactor) and strength (screenProbeOcclusionIntensity). Turning the temporal resampling's reset on (reservoirGatherTemporalResamplingResetHistory) discards the reservoirs of the last image once, at the image it turns on. When the reservoirs of the chosen reduction do not fit the device's largest storage buffer (a 4K image at the default 2), the reduction is raised until they do. Every setting is read again at each image and its default is the reference's.

// Reservoirs gather the indirect light: a ray every third pixel, one spatial pass, validated every eight images to follow a change of the lighting faster, with a wider contact occlusion.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  finalGatherMethod: 'reservoirs',
  reservoirGatherShortRangeAOMaxScreenTraceFraction: 0.03,
  reservoirGatherDownsampleFactor: 3,
  reservoirGatherSpatialResamplingNumPasses: 1,
  reservoirGatherValidateTemporalReservoirsEveryNFrames: 8,
  reservoirGatherUpsampleMethod: 'jitteredBilinear',
})

sampled-lighting-debug-views.title: Sampled lighting: debug views
sampled-lighting-debug-views.description: The views that draw the sampled lighting and the subsurface scattering over the image.
sampled-lighting-debug-views.html:
The sampled lighting (sampledLights) and the subsurface scattering have views that draw over the image, as the other diagnostic views do. They are chosen by world.diagnostic.mode or by a setting, and need the effect they show to be on.

ModeWhat it shows
virtual-shadow-map-shadow-castersover the image, the edges of the box of every placement the shadows keep as invalidating or that may, in the colour of its class (red a static one that deforms, purple a dynamic one that moves or deforms, blue a dynamic one whose offset may invalidate), with the legend of the classes at the lower left; the green, cyan and grey classes draw no box
virtual-shadow-map-clipmap-virtual-spaceover the image in grey, a square that shows the pages the first sun's shadow clipmap has mapped, level by level from the finest to the coarsest, each in the colour of its address and level, zoomed so that the finest level's pages fill it; needs shadows (await engine.setDiagnostic('virtual-shadow-map-clipmap-virtual-space'))
virtual-shadow-map-shadow-factorover the image in grey, the share of each light that reaches the surface: yellow lit, dark blue in shadow, the lights added (the one light shadowVisualizeLightName names, alone); the legend at the lower left; needs shadows and virtual shadow maps (await engine.setDiagnostic('virtual-shadow-map-shadow-factor'))
virtual-shadow-map-clipmap-or-mipover the image in grey, one colour a level: the clipmap level a sun reads at the pixel, or the mip level a local light reads, mixed with the share of light; needs shadows and virtual shadow maps (await engine.setDiagnostic('virtual-shadow-map-clipmap-or-mip'))
virtual-shadow-map-virtual-pageover the image in grey, the virtual page the last ray of the pixel read, in the colour of its address mixed with the colour of its level and the share of light; needs shadows and virtual shadow maps (await engine.setDiagnostic('virtual-shadow-map-virtual-page'))
virtual-shadow-map-cached-pageover the image in grey, the state of the page the pixel reads: green kept from the last image (shown for one light, or for all with shadowVisualizeCachedPagesOnly), red both layers drawn again, blue the dynamic layer alone, yellow-green kept by force; with the legend; needs shadows and virtual shadow maps (await engine.setDiagnostic('virtual-shadow-map-cached-page'))
virtual-shadow-map-ray-countover the image, the rays traced at the pixel against the most the lights trace, from green to red; needs shadows and virtual shadow maps (await engine.setDiagnostic('virtual-shadow-map-ray-count'))
virtual-shadow-map-general-debugover the image, the mean distance from the pixel to what shadows it as a grey (2000 centimetres to white); needs shadows and virtual shadow maps (await engine.setDiagnostic('virtual-shadow-map-general-debug'))
virtual-shadow-map-dirty-pageover the image in grey, the page the pixel reads, red where its static layer was written (drawn or cleared) this image, green where its dynamic layer was; needs shadows and virtual shadow maps (await engine.setDiagnostic('virtual-shadow-map-dirty-page'))
virtual-shadow-map-gpu-invalidated-pageover the image in grey, the page the pixel reads, red where its static layer was invalidated by the casters that moved, green where its dynamic layer was; needs shadows and virtual shadow maps (await engine.setDiagnostic('virtual-shadow-map-gpu-invalidated-page'))
virtual-shadow-map-merged-pageover the image in grey, the page the pixel reads, red where its static layer was drawn this image and merged into the dynamic one, green elsewhere; needs shadows and virtual shadow maps (await engine.setDiagnostic('virtual-shadow-map-merged-page'))
virtual-shadow-map-overdrawover the image in grey, how many times the shadow raster drew the texel the pixel reads this image, inferno from dark to bright, scaled by shadowVisualizeOverdrawScale; needs shadows and virtual shadow maps
rect-light-atlasover the image, the atlas of the rectangle lights' pictures drawn small at the mip level rectLightAtlasDebugMipLevel, a green border round each slot in use, red round the packing's horizon lines, yellow round the free rectangles, and the figures as text (the same as rectLightAtlasDebug)
sampled-lights-overviewthe shadow caster views side by side, in tiles with rounded corners, over the image
sampled-lights-shadow-castersthe surface under each pixel in grey, with the label Shadow Casters, Materials:0, FarField:0, HairVoxels:0 (the traces are made through the distance field, which has no scene of its own to colour)
sampled-lights-shadow-caster-qualitythe same, with the label that names red a missing caster and blue a mismatching one
sampled-lights-complexity-opaquethe light complexity of the surfaces: for the pixel under the debug cursor, the lights of its cell of the light grid sorted by the weight the sampling gives them, each as a row of text (its share of the sum, whether it was seen in the image before, its kind and its name) and a line and a symbol from the pixel to it (a sphere for a point light, an arc for a spot, two rectangles for a rectangle light, a line along its direction for a sun; the light under the mouse in orange), and the image in grey times a colour that goes from blue to red with the cost of sampling each pixel
sampled-lights-complexity-front-layerthe same for the nearest translucent layer (needs sampledLightsFrontLayer)
sampled-lights-complexity-hair-strands, sampled-lights-complexity-volume, sampled-lights-complexity-translucency-volumethe hair strands' and the volumes' light complexity: not drawn yet (the modes are refused, and the setting below writes that the input is not drawn)
subsurface-profilesin the lower right quarter, the whole image's subsurface profile of each pixel: the default skin buff, then red, green, blue, magenta, cyan and yellow, 100 dark green, 255 white, any other mid grey; the profile's number or letter in each cell of eight pixels, all faded where the scattering stays inside a pixel; the title and the list of the profiles are written at the top left
SettingDefaultMeaning
sampledLightsVisualize0A numbered view in place of a mode: 1 the overview, 2 the shadow casters, 3 their quality, 4 and 5 the denoiser overviews (4 by 4 tiles of the views below), 6 the shading confidence, 7 the frames accumulated (red invalid, yellow the first), 8 the upsample mask (yellow: no history), 9 and 10 the diffuse and specular demodulation, 11 and 12 the deviation of each light over its mean (red a disocclusion, blue the spatial filter, violet both), 13 and 14 the history's own deviation (blue above the threshold sampledLightsSpatialHistoryDeviation), 15 and 16 the clamp of the history (yellow fully rejected). Each view is labelled at its foot. The setting wins over the mode.
sampledLightsVisualizeShadowCasterMissingDistance0.5Metres a traced surface may lie behind the drawn one before it is called missing
sampledLightsVisualizeShadowCasterPoorDistance0.25Metres it may lie in front before it is called mismatching
sampledLightsVisualizeTileClassification0The tiles of the classification over the image: 1 the surfaces' tiles, 2 the downsampled tiles (3 to 6 the hair strands' and the nearest layer's, drawn with their own images); each type in its colour with a count table
sampledLightsVisualizeLightComplexity0The input of the light complexity view in place of a mode (a mode wins): 1 the surfaces, 2 the hair strands, 3 the nearest translucent layer, 4 the volume, 5 the translucency volume. Only 1 and 3 are drawn yet
sampledLightsVisualizeLightComplexityMaxLights32The most lights the list shows, the heaviest first
sampledLightsVisualizeLightComplexityMaxCost32The cost the heat map paints red; a lower cost goes through yellow, green and cyan to blue, a pixel with no cost stays grey. 0 paints no heat map
sampledLightsVisualizeLightComplexityFreezefalseKeeps the list and the lines of the last pixel read, so that the cursor and the camera can move; the heat map is not painted
sampledLightsVisualizeLightComplexityDumpfalseWrites the list to the console once each time the option is turned on: name, share and weight, visibility, kind and place or direction of every light
sampledLightsVisualizeLightComplexityHeatmaptruePaints the heat map; false leaves the image as it is
sampledLightsVisualizeLightComplexityLightColortrueThe lines and symbols in the light's own colour, dimmed when it was not seen; false: green, dark green when not seen
sampledLightsDebug0The input the debug prints speak of: 1 the surfaces, 2 the volume, 3 the translucency volume, 4 the hair strands, 5 the nearest layer
sampledLightsDebugTraceStatsfalseWith sampledLightsDebug, the count of rays each trace method got, written at the right of the image
sampledLightsDebugCursorX, sampledLightsDebugCursorY-1The pixel the prints inspect; -1 is the middle of the image
subsurfaceDebugPixelfalseAt full resolution, the lighting of the pixel under the cursor written as a table: its lit colour, the diffuse and specular light rebuilt from it, its profile, base colour, tint and scattered light, and the colour the recombine makes
 
// The frames each pixel's light has accumulated, the tiles of the classification, and the subsurface pixel at the middle.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  sampledLights: true,
  sampledLightsVisualize: 7, // the frames accumulated
  sampledLightsVisualizeTileClassification: 1,
  sampledLightsDebug: 1,
  sampledLightsDebugTraceStats: true,
  subsurfaceDebugPixel: true,
  sampledLightsDebugCursorX: 960,
  sampledLightsDebugCursorY: 540,
})
world.diagnostic.mode = 'subsurface-profiles'

The light complexity view lists the lights of the cell under the debug cursor and paints the cost of sampling every pixel. The list is read back a few frames after the pixel is asked, and the lights are named by their ids.

// The lights of the pixel at (960, 540), the heaviest eight, and the heat map red from a cost of 16.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  sampledLights: true,
  sampledLightsDebugCursorX: 960,
  sampledLightsDebugCursorY: 540,
  sampledLightsVisualizeLightComplexityMaxLights: 8,
  sampledLightsVisualizeLightComplexityMaxCost: 16,
})
world.diagnostic.mode = 'sampled-lights-complexity-opaque'

hair-strands-debug-views.title: Hair strands: debug views
hair-strands-debug-views.description: Four diagnostic views of the hair strands: bounds, statistics and the deep shadows.
hair-strands-debug-views.html:
Four diagnostic views (world.diagnostic.mode) draw over the image: hair-light-bounds the statistics of the strands (the components of the fibre, the voxelization, the atlas of the deep shadows) and the bounds the settings ask for; hair-deep-opacity-maps the same, and the depth and the layers of a deep shadow side by side; hair-macro-group-screen-rect a green frame around the pixels each macro group of strands covers, and one around all of them; hair-voxels-density the strands' count along the ray of each pixel through the voxels, from blue to red, and the box of each volume. The name of the view is written at the bottom. They need hairStrands and a scene that carries strands (the deep shadows a light that casts them, castHairDeepShadow).

SettingDefaultMeaning
hairCastShadowWhenOutOfViewDebugfalsein every view: the view frustum in blue, the bound of each directional light in purple, the box of each groom out of view in the light's space green where it reaches the frustum and yellow where it does not, and in the world in red
hairDeepShadowDebugIndex0rank of the deep shadow hair-deep-opacity-maps draws; it draws nothing past the slots the atlas holds
hairDeepShadowDebugScale20divisor of the layers' values in that view
hairDeepShadowDebugMacroBoundsfalsethe box of each macro group, in the views of the bounds and of the deep shadows
hairDeepShadowDebugShadowBoundsfalsethe frustum of each deep shadow, in the same views
hairVoxelDebugTraversal'linear''linear' a voxel a step, 'mip' through the levels of the pages
hairVoxelDebugDrawVoxelstruedraw the strands' count
hairVoxelDebugDrawPagesfalsedraw the first page that holds voxels along the ray instead, its coordinates over 12 as the colour
hairVoxelDebugForcedMip-1from 0 to 8, the level of the pages every step reads; below 0 the step picks it
 
// The voxels of the strands marched through their mip levels, with the macro groups' boxes drawn on the deep shadows view.
const world = createWorld('viewer', {
  hairStrands: true,
  hairVoxelDebugTraversal: 'mip',
  hairDeepShadowDebugMacroBounds: true,
})
world.diagnostic.mode = 'hair-voxels-density'

three-migration.title: Migration from Three.js
three-migration.description: On the left a complete Three.js program, on the right the engine program that draws the same scene, section by section.

measurement-entry.title: The measurement entry point
measurement-entry.description: Where a witness or an internal session is still nameable — never through the published `trillion3d` entry.
measurement-entry.html:
A page imports trillion3d and never sees a witness or an internal session: createWorld draws with WebGPU, or is refused by name if the machine grants none. The bench and the proofs still need to name a witness — bare Three.js, THREE.LOD, the internal openMeasuredWorld session — and that is the one job of the separate measurement entry point, packages/sdk-browser/src/measurement/measurement.ts.

It re-exports everything the published entry does, plus what a host never needs: openMeasuredWorld/createMeasuredWorldJob (the internal session a world opens on itself), the pages factory webgpuPagesEngine, and measurement-only helpers such as attachParticles. None of it reaches a published world, and none of it is imported by an application.

createWorldJob.title: A world load as a cancellable job
createWorldJob.description: A world has no dedicated job wrapper of its own: `scene.load` is a plain promise, and the generic `createJob` helper turns it into a cancellable one with progress when a host needs the same job contract compilation uses.

architecture.title: How a frame is drawn
architecture.description: The path from your scene to the picture: the pieces that are kept, the pixels that are filled, the light that is added.
architecture.html:
1. Choose the pieces. Every model is made of small patches of triangles, clusters, stored at several levels of detail. Each frame, the GPU picks for each part of the model the coarsest level that still looks exact on screen.
  2. Write who is where. The chosen triangles are drawn once into a visibility buffer: for every pixel, only the number of the triangle it shows.
  3. Paint the surfaces. Then each pixel reads its triangle's material: colour, roughness, metal, normal map. Surfaces of the same kind are painted together, in one pass.
  4. Light, then smooth. Lights and shadows are added, see-through surfaces come last, and temporal antialiasing blends each frame with the ones before it, so edges stay smooth.

When nothing moves, none of this runs: the world keeps the last picture.

The whole path: docs/ENGINE.md.

occlusion-two-phase.title: Skipping what is hidden
occlusion-two-phase.description: Why a wall hides the room behind it for free: the engine does not draw what the last frame proved hidden.
occlusion-two-phase.html:
A town has thousands of objects behind the first row of houses. Drawing them would cost time for pixels nobody sees. So the engine draws in two passes:

  1. First, what was visible in the previous frame. That gives a rough picture of the depth: how far the nearest surface is at each place of the screen.
  2. Then every other piece is tested against that depth. A piece that is fully behind is skipped; the rest is drawn.

The test only skips what is surely hidden: a wrong guess costs a second test, never a missing pixel. There is nothing to set; it is always on.

In depth: docs/ENGINE.md.

cluster-format.title: How models are packed
cluster-format.description: What the compiler writes: small pages of triangles, stored compactly, each one readable on its own.
cluster-format.html:
The compiler cuts a model into clusters of at most a hundred and twenty-eight triangles, and saves each one as a page the browser can read on its own.

  • Positions, texture coordinates and normals are rounded onto fine grids. That makes a page several times smaller than plain numbers, and the rounding stays far below a pixel.
  • Each page says how far its rounding moved a point, so the engine never guesses.
  • Pages are named by their content: two models that share a piece share its page.

The exact layout is in docs/FORMAT.md.

water-pass.title: Water and glass
water-pass.description: How a see-through material bends what is behind it: the engine reads back the picture it already drew.
water-pass.html:
Water and thick glass are not drawn like paint. The engine first draws everything solid, keeps a copy of that picture, and then, for each pixel of water or glass, reads the copy a little to the side, as light bends through the surface.

  • How much it bends and what colour it takes come from the imported material: its index of refraction, its thickness and its tint.
  • The surface also reflects the sky and the lights, more at a grazing angle, as real water does.
  • One limit: a glass does not show another glass behind it.

In depth: docs/ENGINE.md.

memory-pools.title: Where memory goes
memory-pools.description: Two fixed amounts of GPU memory, one for shapes and one for textures, and what happens when a view asks for more.
memory-pools.html:
The engine keeps two pools in GPU memory: one for the pages of shapes, one for the tiles of textures. You set their size with world.budget (chapter 8); the engine never reads the machine to guess it.

  • The coarsest version of every model always stays in, so there is never a hole.
  • When a view needs more than a pool holds, the engine draws with coarser pieces until it fits: less detail, never a missing part.
  • Changing a pool while the scene runs keeps what still fits and lets go of the rest.

In depth: docs/RESIDENCY.md.

texture-compression.title: Smaller textures
texture-compression.description: Textures are cut into tiles, loaded only where the picture needs them, and compressed when that does not change the image.
texture-compression.html:
A texture is an image painted on a surface. The compiler prepares each one at every size, from full down to tiny, and cuts them into square tiles. The browser loads only the tiles the picture shows, at the size it shows them.

The compiler can also store the tiles in a compressed format the GPU reads directly, about four times smaller. It keeps the compressed version only when it looks the same as the original; otherwise the tile stays uncompressed. A tile that has not arrived yet shows a smaller version of itself, never a hole.

In depth: docs/RESIDENCY.md.

shadow-pages.title: Shadows in pieces
shadow-pages.description: Why a moving camera redraws only a strip of its shadows: the shadow map is cut into pages, like the models.
shadow-pages.html:
To know what is in shadow, each light renders the scene from its own point of view into a shadow map: a picture of distances. The engine cuts these maps into pages.

  • The sun covers the view with a few maps, fine near the camera and coarser far away.
  • When the camera moves a little, only the strip of pages that came into view is redrawn; the others are kept.
  • A page that is not ready yet borrows the coarser map, so a shadow is never missing.

In depth: docs/SHADOWS.md.

IDENTITY_MATRIX4.description: Column-major identity, read and never written: the pose of a node or of a root with no pose.
values: Sixteen numbers, column-major.

DiagnosticMode.description: What a frame draws. Availability describes real pipeline outputs, never synthetic overlays: `DIAGNOSTICS` gives, per mode, whether the active renderer can produce it and why not.
values: The lit image, from the glTF materials.
The edges of every triangle the cut submitted, seen through the surfaces: what the frustum, the detail levels, the HLOD and the occlusion test dropped is absent, what they kept shows even hidden.
A filled unique colour per submitted triangle.
Stable primitive/page identity, one colour per cluster.
Level-0 clusters against the coarser DAG reductions actually selected this frame.
Where each HLOD level starts: white an object near, blue HLOD 0 (its own meshes batched, past the main loading range), then yellow, purple and cyan the coarser levels.
The per-cluster error projected through the cluster sphere, as the cut uses it.
One colour per material class: the class pass that resolved the pixel.
Selected visible pages; rejected hierarchy nodes are counted, not drawn.
Unavailable: texture mip residency is not instrumented.
Unavailable: no fragment counter.
Black: the pixel did not change since the last frame. Grey to white: it changed, eight times amplified — whatever flickers lights up.
Only the light the surfaces reflect, from the screen trace and the probes; black where nothing is reflected.
How much sunlight reaches each surface — white: lit, black: in shadow. No material colour.
All the light on a white surface: direct, reflected, bounced and ambient. No material colour.
The normal image without temporal accumulation: the raw image of this frame, its aliasing and noise included.
The image the temporal AA receives, jitter on, nothing accumulated: each pixel shows the rendered pixel it falls in — it shimmers from frame to frame.
How much history each pixel keeps — white: history kept, black: rejected (a change of shading, off screen).
How much history each pixel holds after the update — white: a full history, black: it starts again. Grey: still converging.
The flicker measure — red: its error, green: how many flickers it counted, blue: the transparents' coverage that cancels it.
The shading rejection, white: history kept — red: without the flicker widening, green: with it, blue: spread to the neighbours, what the update applies.
Why the history restarts — red: disoccluded, green: disoccluded and filled with the occluder's motion, blue: off the last screen.
The motion the accumulation sees — red: moving for the flicker measure, green: a pixel animation, blue: the reprojection edge (white: flat motion).
Thin geometry — red: how far the history clamp relaxes, green: a cluster hole region, blue: the coverage history.
White: a material whose history stays responsive — the accumulation takes a quarter of each new image there.

LodQualityId.description: Runtime LOD presets. `pixelError` is the screen-space threshold the exact-cluster selection consumes; `0` keeps the exact leaves.
values: Maximum source detail — `pixelError: 0`, source anisotropy.
High quality — `pixelError: 1`, maximum anisotropy.
Balanced — `pixelError: 4`.

JobStatus.description: Lifecycle of a job created by `createJob` — a compilation, a world creation. A cancelled or failed job disposes the result it owned.
values: Created, not started.
Running; `progress` events carry a phase and a count.
Resolved; `result` holds the value.
Aborted through its `AbortSignal`.
Threw; `error` holds `{ code, message }`.

CapabilityTier.description: What the safety policy decides a session may run, from measured costs. A `SafetyDecision` carries the tier, whether the feature is enabled, the reason, and when it changed.
values: Every measured cost within budget.
A budget exceeded: the feature is reduced.
The safe path, the feature disabled.

GpuTimingMethod.description: How the GPU durations of a stage profile were taken. A per-pass duration says where, never how much: on a tile-based GPU passes overlap and a pass absorbs its neighbours. The frame total is `gpuImageMs`, the envelope — stage durations do not add into it.
values: Native WebGPU timestamp queries.

ColumnKind.description: Storage of one column of the binary manifest. `COLUMN_KIND` maps each column name to its kind, so a reader knows the view to take over the sidecar bytes.
values: Bounds, spheres, errors, culling nodes.
Signed indices — page integers, group levels.
Unsigned counters and offsets.
Raw bytes — SHA objects, preview pixels.

Side-common.description: Which faces of a surface are drawn — every raster, cone, pipeline and blend-plan decision compares against it. Two readers of `packages/sdk-browser/src/scene/materialSide.ts` stand between it and a host: `sideOf(material: HostMaterials): Side` reads what a host material declares, once at the import boundary, the only place naming the host constants; `materialSide(material: HostMaterials): number` returns that host constant itself, for the diagnostic materials still built with the host library.
values: Front faces only (an empty material array gives this).
Back faces only.
Both, for leaves, fabric and thin cut-outs.

prepare.description: Compiles a source scene into the cache the browser reads. Runs the native compiler — the production path — and returns the manifest read from disk, its `metrics` completed by what only the pointer holds (`wallMs`, `pruneMs`). A source whose product is already in the cache is not recompiled: the folder is proven file by file and kept, and `reused` says what was checked (`null` when the job compiled). `resourceBaseUrl` is required: it is the URL the browser will fetch pages and textures from. What each reader does to its source — polygon faces cut as a fan when convex, by ear clipping otherwise — is in `docs/COMPILER.md`.

prepareMany.description: Prepares many models in one compiler process. The compiler runs `workers` jobs at a time and splits `ramBudgetMb` between them. Resolves with the batch summary — pointers only, nothing read back from disk.

createJob.description: Wraps any pending operation in the engine job contract: a snapshot (`JobStatus`, progress, result, error), subscription, and an abort that disposes what the job owned. The operation must support abort through its owner (RAF, readback, …).

detectCapabilities.description: What this machine's WebGPU actually grants, before a world is created: `{ tier, adapter, extensions, reason }`. The tier is `full` with GPU timestamp queries, `degraded` without them and `unavailable` with no adapter. The reason is always given, so an unsupported capability is reported rather than assumed. The public wrapper a world reads is `capability.detect()` — `{ webgpu, tier, features, reason }`, a simpler shape for the same probe.

perspectiveProjection.description: Perspective projection of a camera with vertical `fov` in degrees, ratio `aspect`, near plane `near`, zoom `zoom`. **Reversed depth, infinite far plane**: `near` projects to 1, infinity to 0. No far plane enters here, hence no division by it — which is what buys the depth precision.

createCameraFrame.description: The matrices of a camera frame, allocated once and rewritten every frame: `view` (the inverse of the camera world matrix), `viewProjection`, and `planes`, the six normalised planes of that frustum.

updateCameraFrame.description: Rewrites the frame: view = the inverse of `world` (zero for a singular world matrix), view-projection = `projection · view`, and the six planes of that frustum. One depth convention crosses all three. `far` is the plane **declared by the host**: the projection has none — it is infinite, which is the whole point of reversed Z — but the frustum keeps it, otherwise a frame would suddenly gain every object the camera was not showing. Omitted or non-finite, the far plane stays unbounded.

worldToRenderOrigin.description: Writes `world` with its translation brought back to `origin`. The subtraction happens in the precision of the inputs — the double of the engine world matrices — and writing a single-precision buffer rounds **after** it, never before: that is all that separates a sharp image from one that shivers. `at` is the rank of the first of the sixteen numbers written, so a buffer of many matrices fills without slicing a view per matrix per frame.

matrixAtRenderOrigin.description: Writes `m · T(origin)`: the same matrix, applied to a point referred to `origin`. Only the fourth column changes, and it equals `m · (origin, 1)`, computed in the precision of the inputs before the write rounding.

viewToRenderOrigin.description: Writes `view` without its translation: the view of a camera of the same orientation posed at the origin of the render frame — the exact counterpart of `worldToRenderOrigin`, the relative world already carrying the eye translation.

createEngineCamera.description: An `EngineCamera`: a camera frame plus `world`, `projection`, `eye`, `near`, `far`, `fov`, `aspect`, every buffer allocated once. This is the engine's own camera — no host object crosses into the runtime.

writeEngineCamera.description: Everything a frame reads, derived from the `into.world` already set and the declared optics.

defaultEngineCamera.description: The camera at the origin with fov 50, aspect 1, near 0.1, far 2000, zoom 1 — the fallback of oracles called before the first frame.

readCameraWorld.description: Resolves the host camera's ancestors, copies its world matrix, then applies `writeEngineCamera`. The only translation from a host camera, once per frame; `HostCamera` is a shape — pose, optics, world matrix, the host's own projection — not a type of the host's rendering library. `aspect` is the ratio the view is drawn at when it is not the one the camera declares: a surface capture renders the same camera aside, at the shape of the surface it writes into. The clip-depth convention is the engine's own, composed from the declared optics in reversed depth with an infinite far plane; nothing of the host's is read here.

holdCameraWorld.description: A bit-for-bit copy of an engine camera, nothing recomputed.

enginePose.description: The position and rotation of the drawn frame, read from the engine camera.

multiplyMatrix4.description: `out = a · b`. The thirty-two inputs are read before the first write, so `out` may be `a` or `b`. Each term is the sum of four products with no initial zero — a sum started at `0` would change the sign of a negative zero. **One buffer type only, `Float64Array`, in and out**: a single caller passing a plain array would make the forty-eight access sites polymorphic and every hot loop would pay it, so a caller starting from a host matrix copies it first.

invertMatrix4.description: `out = m⁻¹` by cofactors. An exactly zero determinant yields the zero matrix — a caller that must distinguish this case tests the determinant, never the output. That threshold is the exact zero, not the engine singularity rule, which applies only where a normal is transported. The sixteen inputs are read before the first write, so `out` may be `m`.

composeMatrix4.description: `out = T · R · S`, the quaternion ordered `(x, y, z, w)`. The last row is written `(0, 0, 0, 1)` exactly; quaternion products are doubled by addition (`x + x`), never multiplied by two.

decomposeMatrix4.description: The reverse: a column's scale is its length, and a negative determinant is carried by the `x` axis alone, whichever axis was reversed at the source. A sheared matrix has no such decomposition — the rotation returned is then that of the column-normalised matrix and recomposition no longer yields `m`, a gap identical to the reference's and quantified by the bench.

copyMatrix4.description: Copies the sixteen numbers of `m` into `out`, each at its offset. A loop rather than `TypedArray.set`: on a view `set` costs a native call, and the outputs are not all typed — a host matrix, a GPU single-precision buffer, which is the only conversion.

determinantMatrix4.description: The 4×4 determinant, expanded along the last row like the reference, and that of the linear part alone (the 3×3 block), expanded along the first column. The sign of the second says whether the transform reverses orientation, hence which face a draw must cull. The second is not the expansion of the first: the relative gap is a few ulps, and the signs can differ only near a singular matrix, where neither rounding decides.

normalMatrix3.description: `out = transpose(inverse(3×3 block of m))` on nine numbers, column-major: the matrix that carries the normals of a surface transformed by `m`, shear and non-uniform scale included. The inverse is the reference one, cofactors and product order included, then transposed with no floating-point operation. **On a singular matrix it writes the adjugate, undivided**, not the reference's zero matrix: a singular pose does not erase a surface, it flattens it onto a plane, and the adjugate applied to a local normal *is* the cross product of the transformed edges, sign included — every consumer then normalises. Only a zero, infinite or NaN scale is written apart, as nine zeros.

linearPartScale.description: The engine's one singularity rule, in the form of the WGSL kernel. The scale is the sum of the absolute values of the nine terms of the linear part; the determinant is taken on the columns **divided by that scale before the product**, never on the raw determinant divided by its cube — `t³` overflows past 1e103 and vanishes under 1e-103, exactly where the rule is meant to decide. `adjugateFactor` then returns `1 / determinant` for a regular matrix (the reference bits), `1` for a singular one (the adjugate as-is), and `null` when the scale is not finite and strictly positive, where the adjugate itself must be replaced by zero.

basisMatrix4.description: The columns `u`, `v`, `n` then the origin, last row `(0, 0, 0, 1)`; and a uniform scale `s` placed at `center`. Both replace a two-call sequence of the host library with one write.

dotVector3.description: `a · b` on three components read at `aAt` and `bAt`: one buffer plus an offset, never a view — that is what makes it cheap inside a loop over thousands of vectors.

crossVector3.description: `out = a × b`. The six components are read before the first write, so `out` may be `a` or `b`.

lengthSqVector3.description: `x² + y² + z²`, the three squares summed in the reference's order. `Math.sqrt` of it is the reference's `length()` bit for bit.

normalizeVector3.description: `v / ‖v‖` in place — each component multiplied by `1 / (length || 1)`, so a zero vector is left unchanged.

scaleVector3.description: The three components multiplied in place; `out = a · s` written at an offset; and `out += a · s`.

transformAffinePoint.description: `M · (x, y, z, 1)` without perspective divide — the form of an affine matrix, whose last row is `(0, 0, 0, 1)`. For such a matrix and a finite point this is bit for bit the projective transform, whose `1 / w` factor is then 1. The coordinates arrive as parameters, so `out` may be the input vector.

transformHomogeneousPoint.description: The four homogeneous components, no divide: the point in clip space when `M` is a view-projection. The caller divides by the fourth, after discarding the one that is zero or non-finite.

transformDirectionVector3.description: The 3×3 block of an affine 4×4 applied to a direction, then the reference normalisation — translation ignored, as for any direction. And `M · (x, y, z)` for a 3×3 matrix stored column-major on nine numbers.

srgbToLinear.description: The exact sRGB curve — `c / 12.92` below 0.04045, `((c + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4` above — and its inverse, negatives clamped to zero before the exponent.

hslToRgb.description: Hue, saturation and lightness to three RGB components written at `out[o..o+2]`. The reference `setHSL` term by term: wrapped hue, saturation and lightness clamped to `[0, 1]`, zero saturation returned as grey, then the piecewise ramp. The RGB comes out in the encoding the HSL is given in: no transfer curve is applied.

boxUnion.description: A box is six numbers stored flat from `o`: three lower bounds, three upper. An empty box has its lower bounds at `+Infinity` and its upper at `-Infinity`; a NaN bound does not make a box empty. Expanding and uniting take the bounds as parameters, so no temporary object is built per call.

boxTransform.description: The box enclosing the image of `box` by `m`: the union of its eight transformed corners. An empty box stays as is, bounds included, and `out` may be `box` — bounds are read before the first write. `boxCornersInto` writes those eight corners flat, twenty-four numbers: corner `i` takes the upper bound on `x` when bit 1 is set, on `y` for bit 2, on `z` for bit 4, each corner being the homogeneous transform `(m·p) / (m₃·p)`.

sphereFromBounds.description: The bounding sphere of a box, written flat from `o`: centre `x, y, z` then radius. The centre is `(min + max) * 0.5`, the radius half the diagonal. An empty box — an upper bound below its lower — yields the empty sphere, zero centre and radius `-1`. This is the reference box arithmetic term by term, NaN, signed zeros and infinities included.

frustumPlanesFromMatrix.description: The six planes of the frustum of a clip matrix — a view-projection, or a projection alone for planes in view space. The first normalises them, so `a·x + b·y + c·z + d` is a signed distance; the second leaves the raw sums and differences of the rows, where the sign alone decides, with no square root or division: the form of the exact clip test, where normalising would shift the rounding. A degenerate matrix yields NaN or infinite planes without throwing.

frustumFarPlane.description: The far plane of a frustum whose projection has none. The engine projection is infinite: its depth row no longer bounds anything, so the far plane is read from the **view** matrix, whose third row gives the view depth — a point is inside when `far + z >= 0`. A non-finite `far` leaves the zero plane in place, a truly unbounded far plane.

frustumExcludesBox.description: The box against the frustum: the first is true when a plane leaves all eight corners behind. The second returns three states — 0 outside, 1 straddling, 2 entirely inside — in two passes, the first only rejecting, the second reading the most trailing corner to tell "straddling" from "inside". A subtree entirely inside saves a test on every box underneath it.

createTransformTree.description: The engine transform hierarchy, data-oriented: a node is an index into flat arrays — parent, flags, position, quaternion `(x, y, z, w)`, scale, local matrix, world matrix. `localViews[i]` and `worldViews[i]` are sixteen-number views created at growth and never during an update: the GPU reads the whole buffer, a kernel reads a node's view. A fresh node is the reference's fresh object: zero position, identity rotation, scale 1, identity matrices, automatic update. A growth replaces every array, so a caller re-reads `tree.world` or `tree.worldViews` after an add.

setNodePosition.description: Writes go through the setters, which mark what they changed — that mark is what an update reads to decide whom to visit. Under automatic update the next update recomposes the local matrix from the pose, as the reference overwrites `matrix`; `setNodeAutoUpdate(tree, node, false)` keeps the matrix a caller wrote.

reparentTransformNode.description: Attaches `node` under `parent` (`-1`: a root) like the reference `add` — matrices do not move until the next update — and throws if `parent` is `node` or one of its descendants. Removing takes the node and all its descendants, their indices reused afterwards; to detach a subtree while keeping it, reparent it to `-1`.

updateNodeMatrixWorld.description: The node and its whole subtree, parents first. A node is reached if it updates automatically, if it is marked, or if `force`. The stamp of a visited node is `2 · traversal + reached`, so one read tells a child whether it is in the subtree and what its parent passes it. The second form also walks the ancestors from the root, when asked.

lookAtNode.description: Turns `node` toward the world point `(x, y, z)`. `viewer` is true for a camera or a light, which look toward their `−z`, false for an object, which presents its `+z`. `up` is the node's up, `(0, 1, 0)` by default. Ancestors and the node are updated first.

frustumKeepsBoxBatch.description: `n` boxes of six numbers (min then max) against the twenty-four floats of a frustum: `kept[i]` is 1 where the box intersects or sits inside, and the count kept is returned — `frustumExcludesBox` negated, the polarity the reference answers in. The sphere batch writes `SPHERE_VALUES` numbers per box, centre then radius to the corner, as `sphereFromBounds` does. Both loops live in `packages/math/src/batch/culling.ts`.

boxUnionBatch.description: `into` grown by `n` boxes, or by `n` boxes each transformed by its own matrix first — one pass, one scratch box, no allocation. Both repeat `boxUnion`, the second `boxTransform` before it: the world bounds of a whole scene in one call.

transformPointsBatch.description: `n` points of three numbers by one affine matrix, or one matrix per point; `n` directions by the upper 3×3 then normalised, translation ignored. They repeat `transformAffinePoint` and `transformDirectionVector3`.

scene-editor.title: Build a scene with the editor
scene-editor.description: Add shapes and lights, pick them with the mouse, move them with handles, recolour them, save the scene and open it again — in the portal, on the public API alone.
scene-editor.html:
The scene editor is a page of this portal built on three doors of the engine and nothing else. Start from an empty scene: Add → Box, then Add → Directional light. Click the box: world.raycast finds it under the pointer, and the handles of controls.transform appear on it. Drag an arrow to move it — the camera rests while a handle is held — press E to turn it, R to scale it. Change its colour in the inspector: the engine repaints the material in place, the frame's cost stays in the stats corner. Save downloads scene.toJSON; New, then Open, builds the same scene again with scene.fromJSON.

Every step is undone with Ctrl+Z, and the scene is kept in the browser between two visits. Nothing is drawn or moved by the page itself: what you see is the engine.

pick-with-the-pointer.title: Pick an object with the pointer
pick-with-the-pointer.description: `world.raycast` returns the nearest object under a canvas point: the node the page added, the point and normal hit, the distance.
pick-with-the-pointer.html: The test runs on the CPU over the scene's own geometry: triangle meshes triangle by triangle, a loaded model on its box, lines and points never. Hidden subtrees and helper marks are skipped. See it in Click to pick.

move-with-handles.title: Move, turn and scale with handles
move-with-handles.description: `controls.transform(world)` puts handles on one object; a drag writes its pose through its parents, and the camera rests meanwhile.
move-with-handles.html: Modes translate, rotate and scale, world or local axes, optional steps. The events dragStart and dragEnd frame one drag — one undo step. See it in Move, rotate, scale.

save-and-open-a-scene.title: Save and open a scene
save-and-open-a-scene.description: `scene.toJSON(camera)` writes the scene as plain versioned JSON; `scene.fromJSON(json, camera)` builds it again.
save-and-open-a-scene.html: Shapes are stored by the call that built them, materials by their values, loaded models by their address — never inlined — and helper marks not at all. Another format version is refused by name. See it in Save the scene.

members.rows: The placement rows the linked row belongs to.
members.index: The row's rank in those rows.
members.local: Its mesh's local matrix, relative to the parent: sixteen numbers.

members.shadowedLocals: How many shadow-casting lights are local lights rather than suns.

members.contactShadows: Whether the lights cast contact shadows; `true` by default. Each lit pixel casts a ray of eight steps toward each light through the scene's depth, and is darkened where something stands against it in the light's way; a light casts one if it casts a shadow and its `contactShadowLength`, or the override, is above 0. `false` takes the lights' rays away; the eye and hair models still cast their own.
members.contactShadowOverrideLength: A length that replaces the `contactShadowLength` of every light when it is 0 or more; below 0, the default of -1, each light keeps its own. 0 turns the lights' contact shadows off. Its unit is the one `contactShadowOverrideLengthInWorldSpace` says; the eye and hair models' rays do not follow it.
members.contactShadowOverrideLengthInWorldSpace: Whether `contactShadowOverrideLength` is in metres (`true`) or in screen units (`false`, the default), a share of the screen's height at the pixel's depth.
members.contactShadowOverrideCastingIntensity: The intensity, from 0 to 1, that every light's contact shadow has where its ray meets a surface that casts contact shadows, when it is 0 or more; below 0, the default of -1, each light keeps its own `contactShadowCastingIntensity`. Range -1 to 1.
members.contactShadowOverrideNonCastingIntensity: The intensity, from 0 to 1, that every light's contact shadow has where its ray meets a surface that does not cast contact shadows, when it is 0 or more; below 0, the default of -1, each light keeps its own `contactShadowNonCastingIntensity`. Range -1 to 1.
members.shadowDynamicResolutionTimeBudgetMs: The milliseconds the shadow raster's GPU time may take; from 0, 0 by default, which is off. Above 0, the dynamic resolution fits the raster to this budget and raises every shadow map's resolution bias by the share of that fit its cost takes. It needs the render scale on `'auto'` and a GPU timer, and wins over `shadowDynamicResolutionLoadBudget`. Off, nothing is counted or run.
members.shadowDynamicResolutionLoadBudget: The estimated load of the shadow raster, counted in the clusters it draws, past which every shadow map's resolution bias rises, the busier maps more; from 0, 0 by default, which is off; lower is more aggressive. Ignored while `shadowDynamicResolutionTimeBudgetMs` is above 0. Off, nothing is counted or run.
members.shadowDynamicResolutionPerVsmBiasHistory: The share of a shadow map's compute bias that the frame before keeps when it is eased, to smooth it over time; 0.9 by default, from 0 to 1. Used while a time or load budget is on.
members.shadowDynamicResolutionMaxComputeResolut: The most levels the compute throttle adds to the resolution bias of a directional light's maps, within `shadowDynamicResolutionMaxResolutionLodBias` less the pool's bias; from 0, 99999 by default, which is no cap of its own; 0 never lowers them.
